rankingMethod: User examples first; then close form/setup variations, broader consolidations, and specialist removals. Within each group, editorial priority, category and name. This ranks product simplification proposals, not exercise safety or quality.

candidates.rationale: The listed extra setup is a low block beneath the front foot plus stepping backward; the survivor already supplies the same back-rack, bend-both-knees lunge family.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain reverse stepping and optional front-foot elevation as form notes. The survivor currently steps forward; elevation changes available depth and should not silently become its default.
candidates.name: Front-Foot-Elevated Barbell Reverse Lunge
instructions: Unrack a barbell onto the upper back. Stand on a low, stable lifting block with room to step one foot backward onto the floor.
Keep the front foot on the block and step the other foot back into a comfortable lunge. Keep the front knee tracking with the foot.
Push through the elevated front foot to return to standing on the block. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Unrack a barbell onto the upper back from a squat rack, with the safeties set and room to step forward.
Step forward into a stable lunge and bend both knees. Keep the front foot grounded and the knee tracking with the foot.
Press through the front foot to return to standing, then alternate legs. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: User specifically identified floor press as outside the desired main library. This is the same barbell horizontal-press family, stopped when upper arms contact the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Floor press is a meaningful reduced-range option performed without a bench, not identical to a bench press. Preserve floor setup, gentle upper-arm floor contact, pause, and archived chain-resistance notes; do not assume identical loads or depth.
candidates.name: Floor Press
instructions: Adjust the j-hooks so they are at the appropriate height to rack the bar. Begin lying on the floor with your head near the end of a power rack. Keeping your shoulder blades pulled together; pull the bar off of the hooks.

Lower the bar towards the bottom of your chest or upper stomach, squeezing the bar and attempting to pull it apart as you do so. Ensure that you tuck your elbows throughout the movement. Lower the bar until your upper arm contacts the ground and pause, preventing any slamming or bouncing of the weight.
Press the bar back up as fast as you can, keeping the bar, your wrists, and elbows in line as you do so.

Optional chain resistance: attach matched chains securely to both sides of the bar, clear of the body and rack. Keep track of the bar load, chain weight and chain arrangement separately because resistance changes as chain links lift from the floor.
baseInstructions: Set the bench and rack safeties before lifting. Lie with feet planted, hands slightly wider than shoulders, and shoulder blades supported.
Unrack the bar over the chest. Lower it under control to a comfortable chest-level position.
Press back to the starting position, then return the bar securely to the rack after the set.
Optional grip: a reverse, palms-toward-you grip requires a secure unrack, comfortable wrists and elbows, and suitable safeties or a controlled handoff. Select the load for that grip.

Optional reduced range: use a secure board of known height for a controlled touch, or set matching rack pins for a dead-start press. Brace before each press and do not bounce off the board or pins. Keep the board or pin height consistent when comparing sets.

Optional changing resistance: securely attached matched chains add resistance; overhead reverse bands assist the bar. Keep track of bar load, chains or bands, and anchor setup separately because the same bar load can produce different resistance.

candidates.rationale: This is a step-up with the trailing knee lifted at the top instead of bringing both feet onto the box.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Optional knee drive and per-leg counting; keep the standard support height appropriate to the user.
candidates.name: Step-up with Knee Raise
instructions: Stand facing a box or bench of an appropriate height with your feet together. This will be your starting position.

Begin the movement by stepping up, putting your left foot on the top of the bench. Extend through the hip and knee of your front leg to stand up on the box. As you stand on the box with your left leg, flex your right knee and hip, bringing your knee as high as you can.
Reverse this motion to step down off the box, and then repeat the sequence on the opposite leg.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Place one foot fully on a low stable box whose height lets you step up without hopping.
Push through that foot to bring both feet onto the box, then step the trailing foot down first and return to the starting stance under control.
One ascent and descent counts as one repetition; complete the entered count leading with each leg.

candidates.rationale: The candidate combines a knee tuck, upward leg extension and pelvic curl. Reverse Crunch already permits changing starting leg range.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: An optional upward leg extension precedes the pelvic curl; preserve the controlled curl rather than implying an identical sequence.
candidates.name: Supine Leg Raise and Hip Lift
instructions: Begin by lying on your back on the ground. Your legs should be straight and your arms at your side. This will be your starting position.

To perform the movement, tuck the knees toward your chest by flexing the hips and knees. Following this, extend your legs directly above you so that they are perpendicular to the ground. Rotate and elevate your pelvis to raise your glutes from the floor.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Lie on the back with hips and knees bent near right angles and arms resting by the sides.
Use a small controlled pelvic curl to lift the hips slightly from the floor without swinging the legs or forcing the knees to the chest.
Lower the pelvis under control and repeat.
Optional range: start the legs lower or slightly farther from the torso only while the pelvis and lower back remain controlled. Keep the small pelvic curl central rather than swinging the legs.

A securely positioned decline bench with suitable hand supports changes the resistance angle. Start with a modest decline and retain the same controlled curl and return; a larger leg swing is not required.

candidates.rationale: Reverse Crunch with an ankle cuff and low cable adds resistance to the same small pelvic-curl pattern.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Survivor would need an optional cable/ankle-cuff resistance setup, equipment and load guidance; keep slow pelvic curl, not a swinging leg lift.
candidates.name: Cable Reverse Crunch
instructions: Connect an ankle strap attachment to a low pulley cable and position a mat on the floor in front of it.
Sit down with your feet toward the pulley and attach the cable to your ankles.
Lie down, elevate your legs and bend your knees at a 90-degree angle. Your legs and the cable should be aligned. If not, adjust the pulley up or down until they are.
With your hands behind your head, bring your knees inward to your torso and elevate your hips off the floor.
Pause for a moment and in a slow and controlled manner drop your hips and bring your legs back to the starting 90-degree angle. You should still have tension on your abs in the resting position.
Repeat the same movement for the selected repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on the back with hips and knees bent near right angles and arms resting by the sides.
Use a small controlled pelvic curl to lift the hips slightly from the floor without swinging the legs or forcing the knees to the chest.
Lower the pelvis under control and repeat.
Optional range: start the legs lower or slightly farther from the torso only while the pelvis and lower back remain controlled. Keep the small pelvic curl central rather than swinging the legs.

A securely positioned decline bench with suitable hand supports changes the resistance angle. Start with a modest decline and retain the same controlled curl and return; a larger leg swing is not required.

candidates.rationale: Existing Cable Crunch already supports kneeling, seated and standing; this further splits it by alternating a small oblique twist.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep optional alternating twist guidance and per-side counting separate from the basic straight crunch.
candidates.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch With Alternating Oblique Twists
instructions: Attach a rope to a high cable pulley. Kneel facing the station and hold the rope beside the ears, keeping the hips steady.
Curl the trunk down while gently rotating one shoulder toward the opposite knee. Keep the hands beside the head without pulling with the arms.
Return under control, then repeat toward the other knee. Count each side toward its own selected repetition target; stop at the target rather than continuing to failure.
baseInstructions: Kneel facing a high cable and hold the rope near the shoulders.
Curl the ribcage toward the pelvis without pulling with the arms, then return slowly.

The crunch may be performed seated on a stable bench or standing with a balanced stance instead of kneeling. Position the body under the high cable so the rope stays near the shoulders, then curl the ribs toward the pelvis without turning the movement into an arm pull or hip hinge.

candidates.rationale: Both are barbell wrist flexion with still forearms. Standing with the bar behind the body adds setup rather than a new movement family.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Rename the survivor Barbell Wrist Curl if merged. Behind-body support changes shoulder position and bar handling; keep the seated supported setup as default.
candidates.name: Standing Palms-Up Barbell Behind The Back Wrist Curl
instructions: Take a barbell from a reachable squat-rack position behind the body and stand with arms extended beside the hips, palms facing backward.
Keep the forearms still and curl the wrists upward through a small comfortable range.
Lower under control for each repetition, then return the bar securely to the rack.
baseInstructions: Sit on a bench with a barbell in an underhand grip and forearms supported on the thighs, wrists free just beyond the knees.
Curl the wrists upward while keeping the forearms still.
Lower the bar through a comfortable wrist range and repeat.
A stable bench may support the forearms instead of the thighs. Keep the wrists free beyond its edge and retain the same palms-up wrist curl.

candidates.rationale: Same floor deadlift family with an axle bar; the distinguishing feature is the thick implement/grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep the thicker-bar option and its grip/loading differences as optional equipment notes; historical axle loads must not be treated as directly comparable to standard-bar loads.
candidates.name: Axle Deadlift
instructions: Approach the bar so that it is centered over your feet. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the bar at shoulder width, allowing your shoulder blades to protract. Typically, you would use an over/under grip.

With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees until your shins contact the bar. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back steady, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward.
After the bar passes the knees, bring the bar close to the body, pulling your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward into the bar.
Lower the bar by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.
baseInstructions: Stand with the bar over the middle of the feet.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip it, brace the trunk, then stand with the bar close to the legs; reverse the movement to lower.

Optional changing resistance: matched chains or bands anchored below add resistance; overhead reverse bands assist the bar. Use secure attachments clear of the feet and bar path. Keep track of bar load, chains or bands and anchor arrangement separately.

For a deficit variation, stand on a low, stable platform and keep the bar close through the longer pull. Choose a height that allows a controlled starting position and note that height when comparing loads.

candidates.rationale: Both records are supported cable elbow extensions; this specifies an incline bench and high pulley instead of the survivor’s flat bench and low pulley.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep the high-pulley incline setup and upper-arm angle as optional guidance; do not silently substitute the resistance direction.
candidates.name: Cable Incline Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on incline an bench facing away from a high pulley machine that has a straight bar attachment on it.

Grasp the straight bar attachment overhead with a pronated (overhand; palms down) narrow grip (less than shoulder width) and keep your elbows tucked in to your sides. Your upper arms should create around a 25 degree angle when measured from the floor.
Keeping the upper arms stationary, extend the arms as you flex the triceps. Breathe out during this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Place a flat bench in front of a low pulley with its straight-bar attachment within reach. Take a narrow overhand grip on the bar before carefully lying back on the bench.
With your arms extended, position the bar over your torso. Your arms and your torso should create a 90-degree angle. This will be your starting position.

Lower the bar by bending at the elbow while keeping the upper arms stationary and elbows in. Go down until the bar lightly touches your forehead. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Flex the triceps as you lift the bar back to its starting position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Hold for a second at the contracted position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Optional attachment: a rope may replace the bar, including at a low row-station pulley. Position a stable bench so the cable has a clear path, the attachment is reachable, and the body stays supported throughout.

candidates.rationale: Both guide a barbell from above the chest into a controlled overhead arc; decline support is the title-level extra.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The decline row uses a soft fixed bend while the base emphasizes bent arms. Preserve a comfortable elbow angle and secure setup rather than assuming identical loading.
candidates.name: Decline Barbell Pullover
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with legs secured and take a comfortable overhand grip on a barbell positioned on the floor within controlled reach behind the head.
With a soft fixed elbow bend, guide the bar over the chest, then lower it overhead through a comfortable shoulder arc.
Return along the same controlled path for each repetition. Place the bar securely back on the floor before releasing the grip.
baseInstructions: Lie on a flat bench with a barbell using a shoulder grip width.
Hold the bar straight over your chest with a bend in your arms. This will be your starting position.
While keeping your arms in the bent arm position, lower the weight slowly in an arc behind your head while breathing in until you feel a stretch on the chest.
At that point, bring the barbell back to the starting position using the arc through which the weight was lowered and exhale as you perform this movement.
Hold the weight on the initial position for a second and repeat the motion for the prescribed number of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Same lying dumbbell elbow-extension pattern, with a decline bench replacing the flat bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Decline leg support and changed shoulder angle remain optional setup details; keep the standard flat-bench demonstration.
candidates.name: Decline Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and lie down with a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.

Once you are laying down, move the dumbbells in front of you at shoulder width. The palms of the hands should be facing each other and the arms should be perpendicular to the floor and fully extended. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe in and you keep the upper arms stationary (and elbows in), bring the dumbbells down slowly by moving your forearms in a semicircular motion towards you until your thumbs are next to your ears. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Lift the dumbbells back to the starting position by contracting the triceps and exhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on a flat bench while holding two dumbbells directly in front of you. Your arms should be fully extended at a 90-degree angle from your torso and the floor. The palms should be facing in and the elbows should be tucked in. This is the starting position.
As you breathe in and you keep the upper arms stationary with the elbows in, slowly lower the weight until the dumbbells are near your ears.
At that point, while keeping the elbows in and the upper arms stationary, use the triceps to bring the weight back up to the starting position as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: The movement remains a lying EZ-bar elbow extension with upper arms steady; decline and rack setup supply the differentiator.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain secure decline leg support, controlled setup, and a comfortable lowering point clear of the face.
candidates.name: Decline EZ Bar Triceps Extension
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and slowly lay down on the bench.
Use a decline bench with secure leg supports positioned within a rack. Take a close grip on the EZ bar and unrack it under control above the shoulders, keeping the elbows comfortably in.

As you breathe in and you keep the upper arms stationary, bring the bar down slowly by moving your forearms in a semicircular motion towards you until you feel the bar slightly touch your forehead. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Lift the bar back to the starting position by contracting the triceps and exhaling.
Repeat until the recommended amount of repetitions is performed.
baseInstructions: Using a close grip, lift the EZ bar and hold it with your elbows in as you lie on the bench. Your arms should be perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the upper arms stationary, lower the bar by allowing the elbows to flex. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Pause once the bar is directly above the forehead.
Lift the bar back to the starting position by extending the elbow and exhaling.
Repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both curl one shoulder toward the opposite knee; the decline bench is the main distinguishing setup.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Decline angle increases demand and needs secure supports. Keep per-side counting and avoid forcing elbow-to-knee contact.
candidates.name: Decline Oblique Crunch
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and slowly lay down on the bench.
Raise your upper body off the bench until your torso is about 35-45 degrees if measured from the floor.
Put one hand beside your head and the other on your thigh. This will be your starting position.

Raise your upper body slowly from the starting position while turning your torso to the left. Continue crunching up as you exhale until your right elbow touches your left knee. Hold this contracted position for a second. Tip: Focus on keeping your abs tight and keeping the movement slow and controlled.
Lower your body back down slowly to the starting position as you inhale.

After completing one set on the right for the recommended amount of repetitions, switch to your left side. Tip: Focus on really twisting your torso and feeling the contraction when you are in the up position.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with the lower legs supported on a bench and knees bent. Rest the fingertips lightly beside the head.
Curl one shoulder toward the opposite knee without pulling the neck or requiring elbow-to-knee contact.
Lower under control and complete the selected repetitions on each side.

Optional leg setup: keep the feet on the floor, or rest an ankle comfortably across the opposite knee instead of supporting both lower legs on the bench. Retain the controlled shoulder curl, relaxed neck and per-side repetition target; elbow-to-knee contact is not required.

candidates.rationale: The survivor already includes low/high cable angles and a supported cable fly; this adds only an incline bench setting.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Add a stable incline-bench option with cable clearance and the same softly bent, steady elbows.
candidates.name: Incline Cable Flye
instructions: To get yourself into the starting position, set the pulleys at the floor level (lowest level possible on the machine that is below your torso).
Place an incline bench (set at 45 degrees) in between the pulleys, select a weight on each one and grab a pulley on each hand.
With a handle on each hand, lie on the incline bench and bring your hands together at arms length in front of your face. This will be your starting position.

With a slight bend of your elbows (in order to prevent stress at the biceps tendon), lower your arms out at both sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch on your chest. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Keep in mind that throughout the movement, the elbow angle should remain steady. The movement should only occur at the shoulder joint.

Return your arms back to the starting position as you squeeze your chest muscles and exhale. Hold the contracted position for a second. Tip: Make sure to use the same arc of motion used to lower the weights.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand between cable handles with a stable staggered stance and softly bent elbows.
Bring the hands together in front of the chest, then reopen without forcing the shoulders behind you.
Optional cable angle: use lower pulleys for an upward arc or higher pulleys for a downward arc, keeping a soft, steady elbow bend. Choose a load for the selected line of pull.

For a supported fly, center a stable flat bench between low pulleys, keep the feet planted and bring the handles together above the chest. Arrange a controlled pickup and return without reaching beyond your balance.

For alternating single-arm work, hold one handle steady in front of the chest while the other arm opens and returns. Each arm completes the selected repetition count; use a load that allows the torso and held arm to stay steady.

candidates.rationale: The survivor already allows low-incline or flat chest support; this version changes only the slight bench angle and one-arm execution.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Maintain chest support, softly bent elbows, adequate arm clearance, and a per-arm dose.
candidates.name: Dumbbell Lying One-Arm Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: While holding a dumbbell in one hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench. The other hand can be used to hold to the leg of the bench for stability.

Position the palm of the hand that is holding the dumbbell in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arm extended with the elbow slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the arm with the dumbbell to the side until your elbow is at shoulder height and your arm is roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arm perpendicular to the torso while keeping your arm extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline. Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Extend the arms in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes. This is the starting position.

Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other (to the side) in an arc motion while exhaling. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Optional support: use a low incline or a flat bench with enough arm clearance. Keep the chest supported and choose a load appropriate to that bench angle.

Optional external rotation: add a small, controlled outward rotation of the upper arms as you raise them, then reverse it while lowering. Keep the elbows softly bent and avoid forcing the wrists or shoulders.

candidates.rationale: A seated cable row named for the rope and flared-elbow pull toward the upper chest.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain high elbow path and upper-chest endpoint as optional form; the default lower-rib row must remain clear.
candidates.name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
instructions: Sit on a stable bench facing a low cable pulley with a rope attachment, keeping enough distance for the arms to extend.
Attach a rope to the pulley and grasp it with an overhand grip. Your arms should be extended and parallel to the floor with the elbows flared out.
Keep your lower back upright and slide your hips back so that your knees are slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Pull the cable attachment towards your upper chest, just below the neck, as you keep your elbows up and out to the sides. Continue this motion as you exhale until the elbows travel slightly behind the back. Tip: Keep your upper arms horizontal, perpendicular to the torso and parallel to the floor throughout the motion.
Go back to the initial position where the arms are extended and the shoulders are stretched forward. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Sit tall with feet braced and knees softly bent.
Pull the handle toward the lower ribs, then reach forward under control without rounding or rocking the torso.
Optional setup: use only a secure, load-rated seat riser if extra seat height is needed; keep the feet braced and torso steady.

For a single-arm variation, use a single handle and allow a comfortable grip rotation without twisting the torso. Complete the selected repetition count with each arm and choose a load appropriate for one arm.

candidates.rationale: Both hang from a bar and raise the legs. Hanging Pike adds a tucked start and a much higher shin-to-bar endpoint.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The high-range progression and bent-knee start are more demanding; do not require reaching the bar in the standard.
candidates.name: Hanging Pike
instructions: Hang from a chin-up bar with your legs and feet together using an overhand grip (palms facing away from you) that is slightly wider than shoulder width. Tip: You may use wrist wraps in order to facilitate holding on to the bar.

Now bend your knees at a 90 degree angle and bring the upper legs forward so that the calves are perpendicular to the floor while the thighs remain parallel to it. This will be your starting position.
Pull your legs up as you exhale until you almost touch your shins with the bar above you. Tip: Try to straighten your legs as much as possible while at the top.
Lower your legs as slowly as possible until you reach the starting position. Tip: Avoid swinging and using momentum at all times.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Hang from a secure bar with a steady grip and shoulders controlled.
Keeping the legs mostly straight, raise them forward through a controlled range without swinging.
Lower slowly to the starting hang; one raise and return counts as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: The shoulder-to-overhead strict kettlebell press is unchanged; sitting on the floor with legs apart is the differentiator.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Floor seating removes leg drive/support and increases the need for a controlled upright torso. Keep per-arm dose and use as an optional setup.
candidates.name: Floor-Seated Single-Arm Kettlebell Press
instructions: Sit on the floor and spread your legs out comfortably.
Clean one kettlebell to your shoulder.
Press the kettlebell up and out until it is locked out overhead. Return to the starting position.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Clean one kettlebell to the shoulder and rotate the palm to face forward while keeping the wrist controlled.
Brace the trunk and press the kettlebell overhead without using the legs or leaning back.
Lower under control to the shoulder rack and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.

The palm may face forward or inward at the shoulder, with a slightly outward press path if comfortable. Keep the press strict, without leg drive or leaning back, and retain the same per-arm repetition target.

candidates.rationale: Loaded walking carry with a rickshaw frame instead of separate farmer-carry implements.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain the centered frame handles, pickup/set-down, clear course and apparatus-specific load tracking as an optional carry setup.
candidates.name: Rickshaw Carry
instructions: Position the frame at the starting point, and load with the appropriate weight. Standing in the center of the frame, begin by gripping the handles and driving through your heels to lift the frame. Ensure your chest and head are up and your back is straight.

Immediately begin walking briskly with quick, controlled steps. Keep your chest up and head forward, and make sure you continue breathing. Bring the frame to the ground after you have reached the end point.
baseInstructions: Pick up a dumbbell in each hand with the trunk braced.
Walk through a clear measured path with short steady steps and level shoulders, then set the weights down under control.

candidates.rationale: Both movements place the lifter between side handles to lift a loaded frame from the floor. Rickshaw is a specialized frame choice.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep frame type, handle height and loading convention explicit; do not equate loads across different frames.
candidates.name: Rickshaw Deadlift
instructions: Load the frame with the desired weight. Center yourself between the handles. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hips to grip the handles, allowing your shoulder blades to protract.

With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward. As the weight comes up, pull your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward.
Lower the weight by bending at the hips and guiding it to the ground.
baseInstructions: For this exercise load a trap bar, also known as a hex bar, to an appropriate weight resting on the ground. Stand in the center of the apparatus and grasp both handles.
Lower your hips, look forward with your head and keep your chest up.
Begin the movement by driving through the heels and extend your hips and knees. Avoid rounding your back at all times.
At the completion of the movement, lower the weight back to the ground under control.

candidates.rationale: The bench position and elbow extension match the standard lying dumbbell extension; grip and number of working arms differ.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain a comfortable supinated-grip option and per-arm counting without requiring the unusual grip.
candidates.name: One Arm Supinated Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell above the chest in a supinated grip, using the free hand to steady the upper arm.
Keep the upper arm still and bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell through a comfortable range clear of the face.
Extend the elbow under control and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Lie on a flat bench while holding two dumbbells directly in front of you. Your arms should be fully extended at a 90-degree angle from your torso and the floor. The palms should be facing in and the elbows should be tucked in. This is the starting position.
As you breathe in and you keep the upper arms stationary with the elbows in, slowly lower the weight until the dumbbells are near your ears.
At that point, while keeping the elbows in and the upper arms stationary, use the triceps to bring the weight back up to the starting position as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: This is a supported single-arm lying extension, with a pronated grip and the weight moving toward the opposite upper chest.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Cross-body path and per-arm load/count differ from bilateral lowering near the ears; retain these as optional guidance, not a forced grip.
candidates.name: One Arm Pronated Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell above the chest in a pronated grip. Use the free hand to steady the upper arm vertically.
Bend the working elbow to lower the dumbbell across toward the opposite upper chest through a comfortable range, keeping it clear of the face.
Extend the elbow to return and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Lie on a flat bench while holding two dumbbells directly in front of you. Your arms should be fully extended at a 90-degree angle from your torso and the floor. The palms should be facing in and the elbows should be tucked in. This is the starting position.
As you breathe in and you keep the upper arms stationary with the elbows in, slowly lower the weight until the dumbbells are near your ears.
At that point, while keeping the elbows in and the upper arms stationary, use the triceps to bring the weight back up to the starting position as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: The survivor already allows a palms-in grip; this version only adds a single working arm and a hand on an incline bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve per-arm counting and optional free-hand support without requiring an incline bench.
candidates.name: Standing Palm-In One-Arm Dumbbell Press
instructions: Stand beside an incline bench and hold it with the free hand. Position one dumbbell at shoulder height with the palm inward and forearm vertical.
Press the dumbbell overhead while keeping the trunk steady and maintaining the neutral grip.
Lower under control to shoulder height and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet about hip width apart and hold the dumbbells beside the shoulders, with wrists stacked over elbows.
Press both dumbbells overhead without arching the back, then lower under control.
Optional setup: use a comfortable palms-in grip, or sit on a stable bench with feet planted and the torso supported or held steady. Keep the same controlled overhead press without leaning back.
For alternating presses, return one dumbbell to the shoulder before pressing the other. Complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: The survivor already allows forward- or inward-facing palms. This version specifies turning from inward to forward during the press.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain the optional comfortable wrist/shoulder rotation while keeping the press strict and the per-arm target.
candidates.name: Kettlebell Arnold Press
instructions: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder. The palm should be facing inward.
Looking straight ahead, press the kettlebell out and overhead, rotating your wrist so that your palm faces forward at the top of the motion.
Return the kettlebell to the starting position, with the palm facing in.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Clean one kettlebell to the shoulder and rotate the palm to face forward while keeping the wrist controlled.
Brace the trunk and press the kettlebell overhead without using the legs or leaning back.
Lower under control to the shoulder rack and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.

The palm may face forward or inward at the shoulder, with a slightly outward press path if comfortable. Keep the press strict, without leg drive or leaning back, and retain the same per-arm repetition target.

candidates.rationale: Uses the same supported dumbbell curl but turns palms down for lowering and up for lifting. Grip choice fits the existing consolidation policy.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the supinated-up/pronated-down sequence as an optional method; choose a load appropriate to the lowering grip.
candidates.name: Zottman Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, upper arms supported and palms facing down at the top of the curl.
Extend the elbows to lower the forearms under control. At the bottom, turn the palms upward and curl the dumbbells back up without lifting the upper arms.
Turn the palms downward again at the top and repeat the same sequence.
baseInstructions: Rest the upper arms fully on the preacher pad.
Curl the dumbbells without lifting the arms from the pad, then extend the elbows through a comfortable range.
Optional grip: use palms facing each other for a hammer curl while keeping the upper arms supported; select a load suited to that grip.
For a single-arm variation, keep the working upper arm on the pad and complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: Both straddle an anchored bar and row its loaded end. This row grasps the bar directly rather than using the survivor’s close-grip handle.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A direct two-hand grip changes clearance and grip position; keep the compatible-handle option rather than making it mandatory.
candidates.name: Bent Over Two-Arm Long Bar Row
instructions: Secure one end of the barbell in a landmine and load the free end. Straddle the bar and take a two-handed grip just behind the plates.
Hinge forward with the knees softly bent and the trunk steady. Pull the loaded end toward the lower chest with both elbows close to the body.
Lower until the arms extend, maintaining control of the bar and the same torso position.
baseInstructions: Secure the bar in a landmine attachment and fit a compatible close-grip rowing handle around the loaded end.
Straddle the bar, hinge at the hips and grasp the handle with both hands.
Draw the handle toward the lower ribs, then lower while keeping the trunk still.

candidates.rationale: Same straight-arm front raise, with the torso held on an incline bench rather than standing.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Incline support changes the starting shoulder angle and available range; retain as an optional setup, with a controlled range.
candidates.name: Front Incline Dumbbell Raise
instructions: Sit down on an incline bench with the incline set anywhere between 30 to 60 degrees while holding a dumbbell on each hand. Tip: You can change the angle to hit the muscle a little differently each time.
Extend your arms straight in front of you and have your palms facing down with the dumbbells raised about 1 inch above your thighs. This will be your starting position.

Slowly raise the dumbbells straight up until they are slightly above your shoulders, while keeping your elbows locked. Squeeze at the top for a second and make sure you breathe out during this portion of the movement. Tip: Keep your head resting down against the bench and your legs on the floor at all times.
Lower the arms back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs, with the trunk steady.
Raise both arms together in front to about shoulder height, then lower slowly without leaning back.
Optional range: continue above shoulder height toward overhead only while the shoulders move comfortably and the ribs and torso stay steady. Shoulder height remains the default endpoint.
For alternating raises, return one arm before raising the other. Complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: Kneeling rope row from a high pulley differs by stance, handle and pulling angle, which can be optional cable-row guidance.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Rename survivor Cable Row if approved; preserve kneeling/high-pulley setup and upper-chest endpoint rather than giving seated low-row instructions for every setup.
candidates.name: Kneeling High Pulley Row
instructions: Select the appropriate weight using a pulley that is above your head. Attach a rope to the cable and kneel a couple of feet away, holding the rope out in front of you with both arms extended. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by flexing the elbows and fully retracting your shoulders, pulling the rope toward your upper chest with your elbows out.
After pausing briefly, slowly return to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Sit tall with feet braced and knees softly bent.
Pull the handle toward the lower ribs, then reach forward under control without rounding or rocking the torso.
Optional setup: use only a secure, load-rated seat riser if extra seat height is needed; keep the feet braced and torso steady.

For a single-arm variation, use a single handle and allow a comfortable grip rotation without twisting the torso. Complete the selected repetition count with each arm and choose a load appropriate for one arm.

candidates.rationale: Its instructions describe pulling one overhead handle down to the torso while kneeling. The survivor already includes one-arm and dual-cable pulldowns.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain the kneeling base, comfortable wrist rotation, stable torso and per-side count; do not label this a low horizontal row.
candidates.name: Kneeling Single-Arm High Pulley Row
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and make your weight selection.
Kneel in front of the cable tower, taking the cable with one hand with your arm extended. This will be your starting position.

Starting with your palm facing forward, pull the weight down to your torso by flexing the elbow and retract the shoulder blade. As you do so, rotate the wrist so that at the completion of the movement, your palm is now facing you.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Secure the thigh pad and grip the overhead bar.
Pull the bar toward the upper chest while keeping the torso mostly still, then let the arms extend under control.

Optional grip and attachment: use an overhand, underhand or neutral grip with a compatible bar or V-handle. Keep the pull in front of the body; the standard movement does not require a behind-neck endpoint.

For a dual-cable variation, sit securely between high pulleys with feet planted, hold opposite handles with the arms crossed overhead, and pull them down in controlled arcs, allowing a comfortable rotation toward palms facing each other. Keep the torso steady and handles clear of the head.
For a single-arm variation, use a single overhead handle and complete the selected repetition count with each arm. Attachment and machine changes may require different loads.

candidates.rationale: The cable curl survivor already groups supported lying and preacher-pad setups; this is another supported high-pulley curl.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve high-pulley bench position and stable raised upper arms; keep cable clear of face and bench.
candidates.name: Lying High-Pulley Bar Curl
instructions: Place a flat bench in front of a high pulley or lat pulldown machine.
Hold the straight bar attachment using an underhand grip (palms up) that is about shoulder width.
Lie on your back with your head over the end of the bench.
Now extend your arms straight above your shoulders. Your torso and your arms should make a 90-degree angle and the elbows should be in. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, curl the bar down in a semicircular motion until it touches your chin. Squeeze the biceps for a second at the top contracted position. Tip: As you execute this motion only the forearms should move. At no time should the upper arms be moving at all. They are to remain perpendicular throughout the movement.
Return to starting position slowly.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Face a low cable with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle while keeping the elbows near the sides, then lower under control.
Optional grip: use a rope for a neutral hammer grip or a compatible bar for an overhand reverse grip. These options change forearm emphasis and may need a different load.

For supported variations, lie facing a low cable with room for the handle to move, or use a secure preacher pad to support the upper arms. Keep the body and supports steady and arrange the cable so it stays clear of them.
For a single-arm variation, use a single handle and complete the selected repetition count with each arm at an appropriate single-arm load.

candidates.rationale: Despite its title, the instructions explicitly lie chest-down and lift the arm sideways; this is a one-arm rear-delt fly, not an upright lateral raise.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the chest-down orientation and rear-shoulder movement; add the name as an alias only to the rear fly.
candidates.name: Lying One-Arm Lateral Raise
instructions: While holding a dumbbell in one hand, lay with your chest down on a flat bench. The other hand can be used to hold to the leg of the bench for stability.

Position the palm of the hand that is holding the dumbbell in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arm extended with the elbow slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the arm with the dumbbell to the side until your elbow is at shoulder height and your arm is roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arm perpendicular to the torso while keeping your arm extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline. Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Extend the arms in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes. This is the starting position.

Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other (to the side) in an arc motion while exhaling. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Optional support: use a low incline or a flat bench with enough arm clearance. Keep the chest supported and choose a load appropriate to that bench angle.

Optional external rotation: add a small, controlled outward rotation of the upper arms as you raise them, then reverse it while lowering. Keep the elbows softly bent and avoid forcing the wrists or shoulders.

candidates.rationale: The catalog Bench Jump jumps over a bench, not onto it. Hurdle Hops already covers jumping over barriers.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain over-obstacle semantics and a suitable low obstacle; do not map this to Box Jump, which lands on top.
candidates.name: Bench Jump
instructions: Begin with a bench 1-2 feet in front of you. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Perform a short squat in preparation for the jump; swing your arms behind you.
Rebound out of this position, extending through the hips, knees, and ankles to jump as high as possible. Swing your arms forward and up.
Jump over the bench, landing with the knees bent, absorbing the impact through the legs.
Turn around and face the opposite direction, then jump back over the bench.
baseInstructions: Set up a row of hurdles or other small barriers, placing them a few feet apart.
Stand in front of the first hurdle with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Begin by jumping with both feet over the first hurdle, swinging both arms as you jump.
Absorb the impact of landing by bending the knees, rebounding out of the first leap by jumping over the next hurdle. Continue until you have jumped over all of the hurdles.
Small cones may replace hurdles if they provide a clear, suitable obstacle height and landing space. Count each hop over one obstacle as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: A backward sled drag differentiated by holding the handles overhead rather than low.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain overhead stability and appropriate lighter-load guidance as optional setup; keep backward-path checks and controlled steps.
candidates.name: Sled Overhead Backward Walk
instructions: Attach suitable handles to a sled and confirm the backward path is clear. Hold the handles overhead with the trunk braced.
Walk backward in short controlled steps while keeping the handles stable overhead.
Stop at the selected distance, then lower the handles under control before turning around.
baseInstructions: Load a sled with the desired weight, attaching a rope or straps to the sled that you can hold onto.
Begin the exercise by moving backwards for a given distance. Leaning back, extend through the legs for short steps to move as quickly as possible.

candidates.rationale: Both entries push the same sled forward; sprint versus controlled walking is a pace prescription.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain short faster efforts as a conditioning option, original timed prescriptions and safe load choice; do not convert existing duration targets into distance without an explicit rule.
candidates.name: Sled Push Sprint
instructions: Use a suitable sled on a clear surface with a manageable load.
Brace the trunk, grip the handles, and drive forward with short controlled steps for the prescribed short interval; stop before technique breaks down.
baseInstructions: Place hands firmly on a sled and lean forward with a braced trunk.
Walk it through a clear measured path using short steady steps, then stop with control.

candidates.rationale: Both instructions describe a squat-to-extension throw overhead and backward; one simply has a partner roll the ball back.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Optional partner return; the clear throwing area and backward throw direction remain essential.
candidates.name: Backward Medicine Ball Throw
instructions: Use a medicine ball with a training partner in a clear space with room for the throw and return.
Begin standing a few meters in front of your partner, both facing the same direction. Begin holding the ball between your legs.
Squat down and then forcefully reverse direction, coming to full extension and you toss the ball over your head to your partner.
Your partner can then roll the ball back to you. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand holding a medicine ball with both hands and confirm that the throwing area behind you is clear.
Bend the hips and knees, then extend through the legs and hips to throw the ball overhead and backward.
Land under control if the feet leave the floor. Wait for the ball to stop, retrieve it and reset before the next throw.

candidates.rationale: A cable curl with upper arms held out to the sides at shoulder height instead of by the torso.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain high pulleys and stable raised upper arms as an optional curl setup; resistance angle differs from a low-pulley curl.
candidates.name: High Cable Curls
instructions: Stand between a couple of high pulleys and grab a handle in each arm. Position your upper arms in a way that they are parallel to the floor with the palms of your hands facing you. This will be your starting position.

Curl the handles towards you until they are next to your ears. Make sure that as you do so you flex your biceps and exhale. The upper arms should remain stationary and only the forearms should move. Hold for a second in the contracted position as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly bring back the arms to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Face a low cable with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle while keeping the elbows near the sides, then lower under control.
Optional grip: use a rope for a neutral hammer grip or a compatible bar for an overhand reverse grip. These options change forearm emphasis and may need a different load.

For supported variations, lie facing a low cable with room for the handle to move, or use a secure preacher pad to support the upper arms. Keep the body and supports steady and arrange the cable so it stays clear of them.
For a single-arm variation, use a single handle and complete the selected repetition count with each arm at an appropriate single-arm load.

candidates.rationale: Both are split squats with the rear foot raised; a suspension cradle replaces the bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Suspension is less stable and requires a rated anchor. Preserve it as an optional setup, not the default bench instruction.
candidates.name: Suspended Split Squat
instructions: Secure a suspension trainer to a rated anchor and set one foot cradle around lower-shin height. Stand facing away and place one rear foot in the cradle.
Keep the torso steady and bend the front knee and hip to lower into a comfortable split squat, keeping the front foot grounded.
Press through the front foot to stand. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Place the rear foot on a stable bench and set the front foot far enough forward for balance.
Lower straight down through a comfortable range, then push through the front foot to stand.
Complete the target repetitions on each leg; the entered rep count applies to each side.

candidates.rationale: Quick Leap jumps onto a box then immediately jumps off. Box Jump already documents a repeated-response rebound progression.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep step-down recovery as the standard; describe the jump-off as an optional progression rather than the default.
candidates.name: Quick Leap
instructions: You will need a box for this exerise.
Begin facing the box standing 1-2 feet from its edge.
By utilizing your hips, hop onto the box, landing on both legs. Ensure that you land with your legs bent and your feet flat.
Immediately upon landing, fully extend through the entire body and swing your arms overhead to explode off of the box. Use your legs to absorb the impact of landing.
baseInstructions: Choose a low stable box and stand close enough for a controlled jump.
Bend the hips and knees, jump onto the box with a quiet balanced landing, then step down before repeating.

An optional repeated-response progression jumps down and rebounds into the next jump instead of stepping down. Use a suitable low, stable box only when those repeated landings stay controlled; each jump onto the box counts once. Step-down recovery remains the default.

candidates.rationale: Both catch a partner pass and return it with both hands. The candidate adds a two- or three-point receiving stance and optional running routes.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep any route-running as optional drill notes, separate from normal chest-pass repetition counting.
candidates.name: Return Push from Stance
instructions: You will need a partner for this drill.
Begin in an athletic 2 or 3 point stance.
At the signal, move into a position to receive the pass from your partner.
Catch the medicine ball with both hands and immediately throw it back to your partner.
You can modify this drill by running different routes.
baseInstructions: Stand facing a ready partner in a clear passing area, holding a medicine ball at chest height with both hands.
Extend the arms to pass the ball forward from the chest, keeping the stance balanced.
Receive the controlled return with soft elbows, reset the ball at the chest and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both curl dumbbells with upper arms beside the torso; the survivor already includes grip/path and alternating options.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Seating limits body movement; keep it optional and preserve existing bilateral versus per-arm prescription.
candidates.name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
Rotate the palms of the hands so that they are facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights and start twisting the wrists once the dumbbells pass your thighs so that the palms of your hands face forward at the end of the movement. Make sure that you contract the biceps as you breathe out and make sure that only the forearms move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in and as you rotate the wrists back to a neutral grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Optional curl path: let the forearms angle slightly outward within a comfortable range while keeping the upper arms beside the torso and the seated body still. The path does not isolate a separate inner-biceps muscle.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Optional grip and path: use palms facing each other for a hammer curl, palms down for a reverse curl, or a comfortable outward curl path. A hammer curl can also travel toward the opposite shoulder. Keep the upper arms steady and select a load suited to the chosen grip.

When alternating arms, lower one dumbbell under control before curling the other. Each arm completes the selected repetition count; do not treat the combined left-and-right total as that per-arm target.

candidates.rationale: The survivor already allows seated and alternating dumbbell presses; this row adds one working arm and a supported seat.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Single-arm work uses an appropriate unilateral load and a target on each arm; keep supported seating optional.
candidates.name: Seated Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit upright on a supported bench with both feet planted. Hold one dumbbell and use the free hand to help bring it to the shoulder under control.
Bring the dumbbell to shoulder height. The other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist .
Rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, push the dumbbell up until your arm is fully extended.
After a second pause, slowly come down back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch arms.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet about hip width apart and hold the dumbbells beside the shoulders, with wrists stacked over elbows.
Press both dumbbells overhead without arching the back, then lower under control.
Optional setup: use a comfortable palms-in grip, or sit on a stable bench with feet planted and the torso supported or held steady. Keep the same controlled overhead press without leaning back.
For alternating presses, return one dumbbell to the shoulder before pressing the other. Complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: Both bend and extend the elbow with a dumbbell overhead. The standard already includes seated setup but currently describes a two-hand hold.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Add an optional single-arm hold and per-arm dose; one-arm load is not interchangeable with the two-hand load.
candidates.name: Seated Single-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit upright on a supported bench with both feet planted. Hold one dumbbell and use the free hand to help bring it to the shoulder under control.

Clean the dumbbell up to bring it to shoulder height and then extend the arm over your head so that the whole arm is perpendicular to the floor and next to your head. The dumbbell should be on top of you. The other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist, supporting the upper arm that has the dumbbell .
Rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward and the pinkie is facing the ceiling. This will be your starting position.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head as you hold the upper arm stationary. Inhale as you perform this movement and pause when your triceps are fully stretched.
Return to the starting position by flexing your triceps as you breathe out. Tip: It is imperative that only the forearm moves. The upper arm should remain at all times stationary next to your head.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet about hip width apart and hold one dumbbell securely overhead with both hands.
Bend the elbows to lower it behind the head through a comfortable range, then extend without arching the back.
Optional seating: sit on a stable bench with feet planted and the torso steady or back supported. Keep the same two-hand hold, controlled elbow bend and overhead return without arching the back.

candidates.rationale: Instructions use an overhand bar grip and alternate pulling toward either hand; this is a side-biased pull-up despite the name Chins.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Optional advanced asymmetry and per-side counting. Map to Pull-up, not the underhand Chin-up.
candidates.name: Side To Side Chins
instructions: Hang from a secure pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip.
Pull toward one hand through a controlled range without forcing the chest into the bar, then lower slowly.
Repeat toward the other hand. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Take an overhand grip on a secure pull-up bar.
Pull the elbows down until the chin clears the bar comfortably, then lower with control without swinging.

Optional grip or load: use a stable, load-rated neutral-grip attachment, or secure added weight with a suitable dip belt before starting. Record added weight separately from body weight. Keep the pull in front of the bar; a behind-head path is not part of this default movement.

candidates.rationale: This is an alternating side-biased push-up with the same lower-and-press pattern.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the advanced side-loading option and total alternating-side repetition convention; standard push-up remains symmetric.
candidates.name: Side-to-Side Push-Up
instructions: Assume a push-up position, supporting your weight on your hands and toes while keeping your body straight. Your hands should be just outside of shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
Begin by shifting your body weight as far to one side as possible, allowing the elbow on that side to flex as you lower your body.
Reverse the motion by extending the flexed arm, pushing yourself up and then dropping to the other side.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Count each controlled side lowering and return as one repetition toward the total target, alternating sides.
baseInstructions: Place hands under or just outside the shoulders and form a straight line from head to heels.
Bend the elbows to lower the chest, then press the floor away without letting the hips sag.
Hand spacing may be narrower or wider within a comfortable range. Keep the hands secure and control the same chest-lowering and pressing motion.

candidates.rationale: Single-handle cable row with a staggered standing stance and rotating grip; these are setup choices.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Rename survivor Cable Row if approved; preserve staggered stance, controlled torso and per-arm repetitions.
candidates.name: Shotgun Row
instructions: Stand in a wide staggered stance facing a low cable and hold its single handle with the working arm extended.
Row the handle toward the torso while drawing the shoulder back and turning the palm upward.
Return slowly, then switch the working arm and stance. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Sit tall with feet braced and knees softly bent.
Pull the handle toward the lower ribs, then reach forward under control without rounding or rocking the torso.
Optional setup: use only a secure, load-rated seat riser if extra seat height is needed; keep the feet braced and torso steady.

For a single-arm variation, use a single handle and allow a comfortable grip rotation without twisting the torso. Complete the selected repetition count with each arm and choose a load appropriate for one arm.

candidates.rationale: Seated supported cable pressing changes support, while the retained exercise already provides the same two-handle chest-press pattern.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Rename the survivor Cable Chest Press if approved; retain a supported seated setup as an optional form instruction and compare loads within one setup.
candidates.name: Seated Cable Chest Press
instructions: Place a supported bench between two cable pulleys set around chest height. Sit with your back supported and hold the handles beside the chest with the elbows comfortably below shoulder level.
Press both handles forward until the arms extend, keeping the shoulders and torso steady.
Return slowly to the starting position without letting the weight stack pull the shoulders behind you.
baseInstructions: Position dual pulleys to chest height and select an appropriate weight. Stand a foot or two in front of the cables, holding one in each hand. You can stagger your stance for better stability.
Position the upper arm at a 90 degree angle with the shoulder blades together. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the rest of the body stationary, extend through the elbows to press the handles forward, drawing them together in front of you.
Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.

candidates.rationale: Seated bent-over cable rear-delt fly changes the support and pulley height within the same rear-delt fly family.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep optional seated low-pulley setup, cables clear of knees and elbows held at a steady angle.
candidates.name: Seated Bent-Over Cable Rear Delt Raise
instructions: Stand in the middle of two low pulleys that are opposite to each other and place a flat bench right behind you (in perpendicular fashion to you; the narrow edge of the bench should be the one behind you). Select the weight to be used on each pulley.
Now sit at the edge of the flat bench behind you with your feet placed in front of your knees.
Bend forward while keeping your back flat and rest your torso on the thighs.
Grasp the left handle with the right hand and the right handle with the left before leaning forward onto the thighs. Keep the cables clear of the knees and retain a small bend in the elbows.

While keeping the elbow angle steady, raise the upper arms to the sides until they are parallel to the floor and at shoulder height. Exhale during the execution of this movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower your arms to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions. Tip: Maintain upper arms perpendicular to torso and a fixed elbow position (10 degree to 30 degree angle) throughout exercise.
baseInstructions: Adjust the pulleys to the appropriate height and adjust the weight. The pulleys should be above your head.
Grab the left pulley with your right hand and the right pulley with your left hand, crossing them in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by moving your arms back and outward, keeping your arms straight as you execute the movement.
Pause at the end of the motion before returning the handles to the start position.

candidates.rationale: The working upper arm rests on an incline bench while curling, the same arm-supported pattern as the dumbbell preacher entry.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A securely positioned incline bench substitutes for the preacher pad; preserve one-arm targets and full upper-arm support.
candidates.name: Standing One-Arm Dumbbell Curl Over Incline Bench
instructions: Stand on the back side of an incline bench as if you were going to be a spotter for someone. Have a dumbbell in one hand and rest it across the incline bench with a supinated (palms up) grip.

Position your non lifting hand at the corner or side of the incline bench. The chest should be pressed against the top part of the incline and your feet should be pressed against the floor at a wide stance. This is the starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell upward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms while performing this exercise.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Rest the upper arms fully on the preacher pad.
Curl the dumbbells without lifting the arms from the pad, then extend the elbows through a comfortable range.
Optional grip: use palms facing each other for a hammer curl while keeping the upper arms supported; select a load suited to that grip.
For a single-arm variation, keep the working upper arm on the pad and complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: Single-arm bent-over setup of the cable rear-delt fly, rather than a separate movement family.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain low-pulley setup, hip hinge, soft elbow and per-arm counting; current survivor uses standing crossed high cables.
candidates.name: Single-Arm Bent-Over Cable Rear Delt Raise
instructions: Select a weight and hold the handle of the low pulley with your right hand.

Bend at the waist until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Your legs should be slightly bent with your left hand placed on your lower left thigh. Your right arm should be hanging from your shoulder in front of you and with a slight bend at the elbow. This will be your starting position.
Raise your right arm, elbow slightly bent, to the side until the arm is parallel to the floor and in line with your right ear. Breathe out as you perform this step.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and repeat the movement with the other arm.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Adjust the pulleys to the appropriate height and adjust the weight. The pulleys should be above your head.
Grab the left pulley with your right hand and the right pulley with your left hand, crossing them in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by moving your arms back and outward, keeping your arms straight as you execute the movement.
Pause at the end of the motion before returning the handles to the start position.

candidates.rationale: Both supine instructions slide a heel away and draw it back while the pelvis remains on the floor; the candidate adds a towel and one-side-at-a-time counting.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Towel choice is a sliding aid. Reconcile per-side targets with the base total-alternating count before merging prescriptions.
candidates.name: Platform Hamstring Slides
instructions: Lie on your back on a smooth nonslip-clear floor with one heel on a folded towel and the other leg resting straight.
Slide the supported heel toward the hips by bending that knee, keeping the pelvis on the floor.
Slide the heel away until the leg is comfortably extended. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Lie on the back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Slide one heel away while keeping the pelvis quiet, then bring it back and alternate legs.
Each slide and return counts as one repetition; enter the total across both sides.

candidates.rationale: The movement is a front raise using both hands on one dumbbell instead of one dumbbell in each hand.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve secure two-hand handling and the different load convention; shoulder-height remains the standard endpoint.
candidates.name: Single Dumbbell Raise
instructions: With a wide stance, hold a dumbell with both hands, grasping the head of the dumbbell instead of the handle. Your arms should be extended and hanging at the waist. This will be your starting position.
Raise the weight until it is above shoulder level, keeping your arms extended. Your torso and hips should remain stationary throughout the movement.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs, with the trunk steady.
Raise both arms together in front to about shoulder height, then lower slowly without leaning back.
Optional range: continue above shoulder height toward overhead only while the shoulders move comfortably and the ribs and torso stay steady. Shoulder height remains the default endpoint.
For alternating raises, return one arm before raising the other. Complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: Both entries raise a dumbbell close to the torso with the elbow leading; one side at a time is the only structural distinction.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep a per-arm target and the comfortable shoulder range, rather than forcing a chin-height finish.
candidates.name: Dumbbell One-Arm Upright Row
instructions: Grab a dumbbell and stand up straight with your arm extended in front of you with a slight bend at the elbows and your back straight. This will be your starting position. Tip: The dumbbell should be resting on top of your thigh with the palm of your hands facing your thighs.
Keep the free hand at the waist and the torso steady.

Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbell as you exhale. The dumbbell should be close to the body as you move it up. Continue to lift it only as high as you can maintain a comfortable shoulder position. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbell, your elbow should always be higher than your forearm. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Hold dumbbells in front of the thighs.
Raise them close to the body with elbows leading only through a comfortable shoulder range, then lower without shrugging.

candidates.rationale: A one-arm overhead extension can be an option inside the existing dumbbell overhead-extension entry.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep working upper arm steady and complete the target on each arm; do not impose the two-hand default on historic single-arm work.
candidates.name: Standing One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: To begin, stand up with a dumbbell held in one hand. Your feet should be about shoulder width apart from each other. Now fully extend the arm with the dumbbell over your head. Tip: The small finger of your hand should be facing the ceiling and the palm of your hand should be facing forward. The dumbbell should be above your head.
This will be your starting position.

Keeping your upper arm close to your head (elbows in) and perpendicular to the floor, lower the resistance in a semicircular motion behind your head until your forearm touch your bicep. Tip: The upper arm should remain stationary and only the forearm should move. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Go back to the starting position by using the triceps to raise the dumbbell. Breathe out as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet about hip width apart and hold one dumbbell securely overhead with both hands.
Bend the elbows to lower it behind the head through a comfortable range, then extend without arching the back.
Optional seating: sit on a stable bench with feet planted and the torso steady or back supported. Keep the same two-hand hold, controlled elbow bend and overhead return without arching the back.
