candidates.rationale: The same overhead-to-floor slam is performed with one arm rather than two.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Only use a ball rated for slams and manageable with one hand. Preserve per-arm counts for existing logs.
candidates.name: One-Arm Medicine Ball Slam
instructions: Stand in a clear area holding a ball rated for slams in one hand.
Raise the ball overhead without arching the back, then use the arm and trunk to drive it toward the floor in front of you.
Let the ball stop before retrieving it and resetting. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Use a non-rebounding ball rated for slams on a suitable floor in a clear area.
Raise it overhead without arching the back, then bend the hips and knees as you drive it toward the floor.
Let the ball settle before bending to retrieve it with control. One throw and retrieval counts as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: Both are standing two-hand forward throws from behind the head. The candidate replaces the partner with a rebound wall.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Wall rebound versus partner return changes reception and space requirements; keep the destination explicit.
candidates.name: Catch and Overhead Throw
instructions: Stand facing a suitable rebound wall with a medicine ball, leaving enough clear space to throw and receive the rebound.
Using both hands, position the ball behind your head, using a comfortable controlled reach, and forcefully throw the ball forward.
Follow through and prepare to receive the rebound. Stand close enough to the wall to receive it under control, aiming slightly above chest height.
baseInstructions: Stand facing a ready partner in a clear throwing area, holding a medicine ball with both hands.
Bring the ball behind the head through a comfortable range, then extend the arms and use the trunk and legs to throw it forward toward the partner.
Receive a controlled return and reset the stance before repeating.

candidates.rationale: Both draw the knees toward the torso from supine. Cocoons adds arms moving from overhead and a simultaneous trunk curl.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This is a combined tuck-crunch progression, not just a rename. Keep the standard leg pull-in free of a compulsory trunk curl.
candidates.name: Cocoons
instructions: Begin by lying on your back on the ground. Your legs should be straight and your arms extended behind your head. This will be your starting position.

To perform the movement, tuck the knees toward your chest, rotating your pelvis to lift your glutes from the floor. As you do so, flex the spine, bringing your arms back over your head to perform a simultaneous crunch motion.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Lie on an exercise mat with your legs extended and your hands either palms facing down next to you or under your glutes.  This will be your starting position.

Bend your knees and pull your upper thighs into your midsection as you breathe out. Continue the motion until your knees are around chest level. Contract your abs as you execute this movement and hold for a second at the top. Tip: As you perform the motion, the lower legs (calves) should always remain parallel to the floor.
Return to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Optional bench support: lie on a stable bench with a secure hand support and enough room for the legs to extend under control.

For the seated version, sit securely on a bench with hands holding its sides, lean the torso back slightly and extend the legs. Bring the knees and torso toward each other, then return without rocking beyond control. Each draw-in and return remains one repetition.

candidates.rationale: The same overhead-bell side hinge, adding a second bell picked up by the free hand.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The extra loaded hand changes balance and load; preserve unilateral side count and note the two-bell progression rather than making it default.
candidates.name: Double Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Place a kettlebell in front of your front foot and clean and press a kettlebell overhead with your opposite arm. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward.

Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the locked out kettlebell.
Bending at the hip to one side, sticking your butt out, slowly lean until you can retrieve the kettlebell from the floor. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell that you hold over your head at all times.
Pause for a second after retrieving the kettlebell from the ground and reverse the motion back to the starting position.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Place a kettlebell in front of your lead foot and clean and press it overhead with your opposite arm. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward. Press it overhead by extending the elbow.

Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the locked out kettlebell. Bending at the hip to one side, sticking your butt out, slowly lean only as far as you can maintain the loaded arm upright and the torso controlled. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell that you hold over your head at all times.
Pause for a second at the end of the comfortable reach and reverse the motion back to the starting position.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

Optional balance progression: place the free arm behind the back instead of reaching it downward. Use only the hinge range that keeps the loaded arm upright and the trunk controlled; the per-side repetition target is unchanged.

candidates.rationale: Instructions describe a standard floor glute bridge with a band held across the hips by rack anchors.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Band resistance and secure low anchors are optional loading details; do not introduce rack equipment to the default bodyweight bridge.
candidates.name: Hip Lift with Band
instructions: Lie on your back inside a rack with the knees bent and feet planted. Secure a band across the front of the hips to rated low anchors on both sides of the rack so it cannot slip.
Press through the feet and raise the hips until the torso and thighs form a comfortable line, keeping the ribs down.
Lower slowly to the floor without allowing the band to move out of position.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Press through the feet to lift the hips until the trunk and thighs align, then lower without arching the lower back.
Optional setup cue: gently tilt the pelvis to bring the ribs and pelvis into alignment before lifting the hips. Keep the tilt small rather than forcing the lower back into the floor.

candidates.rationale: Both perform controlled trunk/back extension; this row adds an exercise ball and a plate held at the chest.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The ball is less fixed than the standard extension bench, and load is optional in the generic family. Preserve support/equipment choice and load metadata if merging; do not assume identical range or stability.
candidates.name: Weighted Ball Hyperextension
instructions: Lie with the torso supported on an exercise ball and feet firmly grounded. Hold a weight plate securely against the upper chest with both hands.
Raise the torso through a controlled comfortable back-extension range without throwing the head backward.
Pause briefly, lower under control and repeat.
baseInstructions: Adjust the pad below the hip crease and brace the legs.
Hinge forward at the hips, then return until the trunk is in line with the legs without leaning backward.

candidates.rationale: Both are small band-resisted steps from a shallow squat; Monster Walk chooses forward/backward diagonals and two band positions.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Direction, band position and per-side step counting differ. Preserve an explicit optional diagonal-walk cue and reconcile the base paired-step count.
candidates.name: Monster Walk
instructions: Place resistance bands around the ankles and just above the knees. Stand with the feet apart and knees softly bent so the bands have light tension.
Take small diagonal steps forward, keeping the knees aligned with the feet and the torso steady. Return with controlled backward steps.
Each step by one foot counts toward that side’s target. Complete the selected steps on each side, keeping enough room to turn or reverse.
baseInstructions: Place a loop band above the knees and soften the hips and knees.
Take a small step sideways, then move the following foot toward it while keeping tension on the band and knees aligned.
One leading step and following step counts as one repetition; split the entered total equally between travel directions.

candidates.rationale: Instructions keep the upper arms in line with the torso above the head and extend the elbows, matching the overhead barbell-extension family.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Inclined back support changes shoulder orientation relative to gravity. Rename the survivor Barbell Overhead Triceps Extension and retain a supported incline option if approved.
candidates.name: Incline Barbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms down) that is a little closer together than shoulder width.
Lie back on an incline bench set at any angle between 45-75-degrees.
Bring the bar overhead with your arms extended and elbows in. The arms should be in line with the torso above the head. This will be your starting position.

Now lower the bar in a semicircular motion behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Inhale as you perform this movement. Tip: Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your head at all times. Only the forearms should move.
Return to the starting position as you breathe out and you contract the triceps. Hold the contraction for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand with a straight barbell held overhead in a close overhand grip, feet comfortably apart and trunk braced.
Keep the upper arms steady and bend the elbows to lower the bar behind the head through a comfortable range.
Extend the elbows to return overhead, then repeat under control.

candidates.rationale: Dumbbell curls with arms hanging from a chest-supported incline position add a specific support setup.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Shoulder angle and chest support alter the experience; preserve optional supported setup and do not confuse this with the supine incline curl.
candidates.name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
instructions: Grab a dumbbell on each hand and lie face down on an incline bench with your shoulders near top of the incline. Your knees can rest on the seat or your legs can be straddled to the sides .
Let your arms extend and hang naturally in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the floor.
Now keep your elbows in by your side and face the palms forward. This will be your starting position.

Raise the dumbbells by contracting the biceps until your arms are fully flexed. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and ensure that only the forearms move. The upper arms should remain stationary at all times.
Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Optional grip and path: use palms facing each other for a hammer curl, palms down for a reverse curl, or a comfortable outward curl path. A hammer curl can also travel toward the opposite shoulder. Keep the upper arms steady and select a load suited to the chosen grip.

When alternating arms, lower one dumbbell under control before curling the other. Each arm completes the selected repetition count; do not treat the combined left-and-right total as that per-arm target.

candidates.rationale: A straight-bar curl performed chest-down with arms hanging, already permitting several support benches in its instructions.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Chest support/shoulder position and a reachable pickup or handoff matter. Keep these as an optional supported curl setup, not the standard standing method.
candidates.name: Spider Curl
instructions: Lean chest down against the preacher bench support and take a straight barbell from secure reachable rests or a controlled handoff. Let the arms hang with a comfortable underhand grip.
Curl the bar while keeping the upper arms still and the chest supported.
Lower under control and return the bar to its support after the selected repetitions.

A secure incline bench or raised flat bench may replace the preacher support. Support the chest, allow the arms to hang freely, and ensure the bar clears the bench and floor throughout. Use reachable rests or a controlled handoff for setup and return.
baseInstructions: Stand tall with an underhand grip on the bar.
Bend the elbows while keeping the upper arms near the sides, then lower without swinging the torso.
Optional grip: use an overhand grip for a reverse curl while keeping the upper arms steady. Choose the load for that grip; it may differ from the underhand curl.

candidates.rationale: A horizontal dumbbell press made unusually specific by shoulders-only bench support, lowered hips, and both hands under one dumbbell.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This is a different support and load arrangement, not the normal two-dumbbell press. Keep standard full-back support as the default and preserve historical setup information only as appropriate.
candidates.name: Cross-Bench Single-Dumbbell Press
instructions: Place a dumbbell standing up on a flat bench.

Ensuring that the dumbbell stays securely placed at the top of the bench, lie perpendicular to the bench with only your shoulders lying on the surface. Hips should be below the bench and your legs bent with your feet firmly on the floor.

Grasp the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight over your chest at arm's length. Both palms should be pressing against the underside of the sides of the dumbbell. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by lowering the dumbbell to your chest.
Return to the starting position by extending the elbows.
baseInstructions: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on top of your thighs. The palms of your hands will be facing each other.
Then, using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells up, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width.

Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. The dumbbells should be just to the sides of your chest, with your upper arm and forearm creating a 90 degree angle. Be sure to maintain full control of the dumbbells at all times. This will be your starting position.

Then, as you breathe out, use your chest to push the dumbbells up. Lock your arms at the top of the lift and squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then begin coming down slowly. Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as raising it.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

For a single-arm variation, secure one dumbbell at the shoulder with a controlled two-hand setup, then press and lower it without rolling the torso. Keep the feet planted, use a load suited to the uneven support demand, and complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: The box jump pattern is performed sideways rather than forward.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Lateral landing is a distinct progression; default remains forward. Preserve alternating-direction counting if consolidated.
candidates.name: Lateral Box Jump
instructions: Stand beside a low stable box. Bend the knees and hips slightly, then jump sideways onto the middle of the box.
Land softly with both feet supported and regain balance. Step down carefully on the other side before repeating in the opposite direction.
Each landing on the box is one repetition toward the total target; alternate the direction of travel.
baseInstructions: Choose a low stable box and stand close enough for a controlled jump.
Bend the hips and knees, jump onto the box with a quiet balanced landing, then step down before repeating.

An optional repeated-response progression jumps down and rebounds into the next jump instead of stepping down. Use a suitable low, stable box only when those repeated landings stay controlled; each jump onto the box counts once. Step-down recovery remains the default.

candidates.rationale: A barbell curl with the elbows moving backward and the bar kept against the torso, rather than upper arms held beside the body.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This path is materially different from the strict base curl. Keep it optional with a suitable load; do not rewrite the base to require dragging.
candidates.name: Drag Curl
instructions: Grab a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing forward) and get your elbows close to your torso and back. This will be your starting position.

As you exhale, curl the bar up while keeping the elbows to the back as you "Drag" the bar up by keeping it in contact with your torso. Tip: As you can see, you will not be keeping the elbows pinned to your sides, but instead you will be bringing them back. Also, do not lift your shoulders.
Slowly go back to the starting position as you keep the bar in contact with the torso at all times.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand tall with an underhand grip on the bar.
Bend the elbows while keeping the upper arms near the sides, then lower without swinging the torso.
Optional grip: use an overhand grip for a reverse curl while keeping the upper arms steady. Choose the load for that grip; it may differ from the underhand curl.

candidates.rationale: User’s floor-press preference applies to this dumbbell version too; its upper-arm floor contact truncates the standard horizontal press.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain floor support and pause as optional reduced-range guidance. A floor setup needs no bench and loads/range should not be assumed identical.
candidates.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
instructions: Lay on the floor holding dumbbells in your hands. Your knees can be bent. Begin with the weights fully extended above you.
Lower the dumbbells until the upper arms lightly contact the floor, keeping the elbows comfortably close to the torso.
Pause at the bottom, and then bring the weight together at the top by extending through the elbows.
baseInstructions: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on top of your thighs. The palms of your hands will be facing each other.
Then, using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells up, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width.

Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. The dumbbells should be just to the sides of your chest, with your upper arm and forearm creating a 90 degree angle. Be sure to maintain full control of the dumbbells at all times. This will be your starting position.

Then, as you breathe out, use your chest to push the dumbbells up. Lock your arms at the top of the lift and squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then begin coming down slowly. Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as raising it.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

For a single-arm variation, secure one dumbbell at the shoulder with a controlled two-hand setup, then press and lower it without rolling the torso. Keep the feet planted, use a load suited to the uneven support demand, and complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: The survivor already groups supinated, hammer, and reverse grips. Zottman combines palms-up lifting with palms-down lowering in one repetition.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the changing grip sequence and lighter load as appropriate; a reverse lowering phase is a method, not identical to a full reverse curl.
candidates.name: Zottman Curl
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
Make sure the palms of the hands are facing each other. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Your wrist should rotate so that you have a supinated (palms up) grip. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Now during the contracted position, rotate your wrist until you now have a pronated (palms facing down) grip with the thumb at a higher position than the pinky.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back down using the pronated grip.
As the dumbbells close your thighs, start rotating the wrist so that you go back to a neutral (palms facing your body) grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Optional grip and path: use palms facing each other for a hammer curl, palms down for a reverse curl, or a comfortable outward curl path. A hammer curl can also travel toward the opposite shoulder. Keep the upper arms steady and select a load suited to the chosen grip.

When alternating arms, lower one dumbbell under control before curling the other. Each arm completes the selected repetition count; do not treat the combined left-and-right total as that per-arm target.

candidates.rationale: The standard barbell curl already includes overhand curls. This row uses the rim of a plate for the same elbow-curl direction.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A plate rim changes grip demands and available load. Retain the alternative equipment option and comfortable secure grip rather than prescribe precise clock-face finger positions.
candidates.name: Reverse Plate Curls
instructions: Start by standing straight with a weighted plate held by both hands and arms fully extended. Use a pronated grip (palms facing down) and make sure your fingers grab the rough side of the plate while your thumb grabs the smooth side. Note: For the best results, grab the weighted plate at an 11:00 and 1:00 o'clock position.
Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other and the weighted plate should be near the groin area. This is the starting position.

Slowly lift the plate up while keeping the elbows in and the upper arms stationary until your biceps and forearms touch while exhaling. The plate should be evenly aligned with your torso at this point.
Feel the contraction for a second and begin to lower the weight back down to the starting position while inhaling
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand tall with an underhand grip on the bar.
Bend the elbows while keeping the upper arms near the sides, then lower without swinging the torso.
Optional grip: use an overhand grip for a reverse curl while keeping the upper arms steady. Choose the load for that grip; it may differ from the underhand curl.

candidates.rationale: Both extend and close the fingers around a retained weight; plates at the sides replace a barbell held in front.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The finger-flexion pattern survives, but rim grip and neutral arm position differ. Preserve the plate option and do not map it to the timed Plate Pinch hold.
candidates.name: Standing Olympic Plate Hand Squeeze
instructions: To begin, stand straight while holding a weight plate by the ridge at arm's length in each hand using a neutral grip (palms facing in). You feet should be shoulder width apart from each other. This will be your starting position.
Lower the plates until the fingers are nearly extended but can still hold weights. Inhale as you lower the plates.
Now raise the plates back to the starting position as you exhale by closing your hands.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions prescribed in your program.
baseInstructions: Hold a barbell with both hands and your palms facing up; hands spaced about shoulder width.
Place your feet flat on the floor, at a distance that is slightly wider than shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Lower the bar as far as possible by extending the fingers. Allowing the bar to roll down the hands, catch the bar with the final joint in the fingers.
Now curl bar up as high as possible by closing your hands while exhaling. Hold the contraction at the top.
Count one controlled finger opening and closing as one repetition. Keep enough finger contact to retain the bar throughout.

candidates.rationale: Same front shoulder-raise pattern with both hands on a plate instead of one dumbbell in each hand.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep the plate as an equipment option and its total-load convention; do not imply a single plate and two dumbbells use the same logged weight.
candidates.name: Front Plate Raise
instructions: While standing straight, hold a barbell plate in both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions. Your palms should be facing each other and your arms should be extended with a small steady bend at the elbows and the plate should be down near your waist in front of you as far as you can go. Tip: Keep the elbow angle steady throughout the exercise. This will be your starting position.

Slowly raise the plate as you exhale until it is a little above shoulder level. Hold the contraction for a second. Tip: make sure that you do not swing the weight or bend at the elbows. Your torso should remain stationary throughout the movement as well.
As you inhale, slowly lower the plate back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs, with the trunk steady.
Raise both arms together in front to about shoulder height, then lower slowly without leaning back.
Optional range: continue above shoulder height toward overhead only while the shoulders move comfortably and the ribs and torso stay steady. Shoulder height remains the default endpoint.
For alternating raises, return one arm before raising the other. Complete the selected repetition count with each arm.

candidates.rationale: Both alternate knees toward the torso from a plank. The candidate holds a low push-up and sends the knee toward the same-side elbow.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Low bent-elbow support increases upper-body demand; preserve duration measurement and use the high-plank climber as the standard.
candidates.name: Low-Plank Spider Knee Drive
instructions: Take a low push-up position with elbows bent and the trunk in a steady line.
Bring one knee toward the same-side elbow, then return that leg and repeat with the other knee without advancing across the floor.
Continue alternating under control for the selected total duration, without a separate per-side interval.
baseInstructions: Start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders.
Bring one knee toward the chest, return it, and alternate at a pace that keeps the trunk steady.

candidates.rationale: The bar begins on rack pins at knee or thigh height instead of the floor; the base already combines deficit and resistance-method variations.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Pin height changes the practiced range and load. Preserve rack setup, dead-start reset, and pin-height/band notes as an optional partial pull.
candidates.name: Rack Pulls
instructions: Set up in a power rack with the bar on the pins. The pins should be set to the desired point; just below the knees, just above, or in the mid thigh position. Position yourself against the bar in proper deadlifting position. Your feet should be under your hips, your grip shoulder width, back arched, and hips back to engage the hamstrings. Since the weight is typically heavy, you may use a mixed grip, a hook grip, or use straps to aid in holding the weight.
With your head looking forward, extend through the hips and knees, pulling the weight up and back until lockout. Be sure to pull your shoulders back as you complete the movement.
Return the weight to the pins and repeat.

Optional band resistance: use matched bands secured below the bar and clear of the feet, bar path and rack pins. Keep track of bar load, band arrangement and pin height separately, since each changes the demand.
baseInstructions: Stand with the bar over the middle of the feet.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip it, brace the trunk, then stand with the bar close to the legs; reverse the movement to lower.

Optional changing resistance: matched chains or bands anchored below add resistance; overhead reverse bands assist the bar. Use secure attachments clear of the feet and bar path. Keep track of bar load, chains or bands and anchor arrangement separately.

For a deficit variation, stand on a low, stable platform and keep the bar close through the longer pull. Choose a height that allows a controlled starting position and note that height when comparing loads.

candidates.rationale: Both alternate opposite shoulder and knee. The candidate returns the working leg to the floor rather than keeping both legs cycling in the air.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The floor-resting leg lowers sustained demand. Preserve the easier option and total alternating-side count.
candidates.name: Cross-Body Crunch
instructions: Lie flat on your back and bend your knees about 60 degrees.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and place your hands loosely behind your head. This will be your starting position.

Now curl up and bring your right elbow and shoulder across your body while bring your left knee in toward your left shoulder at the same time. Reach with your elbow and try to touch your knee. Exhale as you perform this movement. Tip: Try to bring your shoulder up towards your knee rather than just your elbow and remember that the key is to contract the abs as you perform the movement; not just to move the elbow.
Now go back down to the starting position as you inhale and repeat with the left elbow and the right knee.
Continue alternating in this manner until all prescribed repetitions are done.
Count each cross-body crunch as one repetition toward the total target, alternating sides.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back and lift the shoulder blades gently.
Bring one knee toward the opposite shoulder as the other leg extends, alternating slowly without pulling the neck.
Count each completed side as one repetition; the entered count is the total across both sides.

candidates.rationale: Both push explosively until the hands leave the floor; the candidate adds repeated rotational landings around a circle.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Rotation is substantially more demanding. Prefer retiring the circle drill while retaining the standard plyometric push-up; do not make rotation compulsory.
candidates.name: Clock Push-Up
instructions: Move into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your hands and toes.
Your arms should be fully extended with the hands around shoulder width. Keep your body straight throughout the movement. This will be your starting position.
Descend by flexing at the elbow, lowering your chest toward the ground.
At the bottom, reverse the motion by pushing yourself up through elbow extension as quickly as possible until you are air borne. Aim to "jump" 12-18 inches to one side.
As you accelerate up, move your outside foot away from your direction of travel. Leaving the ground, shift your body about 30 degrees for the next repetition.
Return to the starting position and repeat the exercise, working all the way around until you are back where you started.
Count each push-up and controlled rotational landing as one repetition. Stop at the selected target; a full circle is not required.
baseInstructions: Take a push-up position with hands just outside shoulder width and the body in a straight line.
Lower under control, then press strongly enough for the hands to leave the floor without adding a clap.
Land softly through the hands and elbows and reset the body alignment before the next repetition.

candidates.rationale: Same back-rack hip hinge performed from a box, removing the standing leg contribution.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Seated support substantially changes hip range and leverage; preserve it as a specialist option and do not compare loads directly.
candidates.name: Seated Good Mornings
instructions: Sit on a stable box inside a squat rack with the bar supported across the upper back and rack pins set to limit the descent.
Brace the trunk and hinge forward at the hips only through a comfortable range while keeping the back steady.
Return upright without leaning back, then rerack securely after the selected repetitions.
baseInstructions: Begin with a bar on a rack at shoulder height. Rack the bar across the rear of your shoulders as you would a power squat, not on top of your shoulders. Keep your back tight, shoulder blades pinched together, and your knees slightly bent. Step back from the rack.
Begin by bending at the hips, moving them back as you bend over to near parallel. Keep your back arched and your cervical spine in proper alignment.
Reverse the motion by extending through the hips with your glutes and hamstrings. Continue until you have returned to the starting position.

Keep a soft, nearly steady knee bend rather than locking the knees. For a dead-start variation, set matching rack pins to a controlled hinge height, position the bar securely across the upper back and brace before standing. Return gently to the pins and reset without bouncing.

candidates.rationale: Both are dumbbell rear-shoulder fly movements with the torso inclined; the seated version hinges without chest support.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The survivor is chest-supported and this one is not. Make support an optional setup while preserving the same rear-delt arm path.
candidates.name: Seated Bent-Over Rear Delt Raise
instructions: Place a couple of dumbbells looking forward in front of a flat bench.
Sit on the end of the bench with your legs together and the dumbbells behind your calves.
Bend at the waist while keeping the back straight in order to pick up the dumbbells. The palms of your hands should be facing each other as you pick them. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your torso forward and stationary, and the arms slightly bent at the elbows, lift the dumbbells straight to the side until both arms are parallel to the floor. Exhale as you lift the weights. (Note: avoid swinging the torso or bringing the arms back as opposed to the side.)
After a one second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline. Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Extend the arms in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes. This is the starting position.

Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other (to the side) in an arc motion while exhaling. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Optional support: use a low incline or a flat bench with enough arm clearance. Keep the chest supported and choose a load appropriate to that bench angle.

Optional external rotation: add a small, controlled outward rotation of the upper arms as you raise them, then reverse it while lowering. Keep the elbows softly bent and avoid forcing the wrists or shoulders.

candidates.rationale: This is shoulder abduction performed side-lying on an incline bench rather than standing.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Bench angle changes resistance across the range; it is not mechanically identical. Keep per-arm dose and optional supported setup only if the library intentionally combines these.
candidates.name: One-Arm Incline Lateral Raise
instructions: Lie on one side against an incline bench and hold a dumbbell in the uppermost hand with a soft bend in the elbow.
Raise the working arm toward the ceiling through a comfortable shoulder range while keeping the torso supported and still.
Lower under control and complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Stand tall with softly bent elbows and dumbbells by the sides.
Lift the arms out to about shoulder height, then lower without shrugging or swinging.

Optional raise path: for scaption, raise the arms in a comfortable diagonal slightly forward of a directly sideways raise, with thumbs angled upward. Keep the same controlled shoulder-height finish instead of forcing a strict sideways path.
The raise may be performed seated on a stable bench or one arm at a time with the free hand on a stable support. For one-arm work, each arm completes the selected repetition count.

candidates.rationale: The catalog entry is a towel-assisted asymmetric chin-up, distinguished by how the spare hand assists.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This is an advanced one-arm progression, not the ordinary beginner Band-Assisted Pull-Up; preserve towel-anchor and per-arm context.
candidates.name: Towel-Assisted One-Arm Chin-Up
instructions: Drape a strong towel securely over a pull-up bar. Hold the bar with one hand and the towel with the other, using the towel hand for assistance.
Pull upward under control while keeping the trunk steady, using only as much towel assistance as needed.
Lower slowly and complete the selected repetitions with each hand as the main bar grip.
baseInstructions: Take an underhand grip on a secure bar and begin from a controlled hang.
Pull the elbows toward the ribs to raise the chin, then lower without kicking.

For a practiced chest-to-bar progression, lean the torso back under control and draw the lower chest toward the bar through a comfortable range. Do not force chest contact or neck extension; return to a controlled hang. The default remains the upright chin-up.

candidates.rationale: The instructions describe a horizontal bar press with elbows in; the curved bar is the main differentiator.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Equipment changes from EZ bar to straight bar, so retain the EZ-bar option and load/setup differences rather than replacing users’ equipment assumption silently.
candidates.name: EZ-Bar Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with an EZ bar loaded to an appropriate weight.
Using a comfortable grip lift the bar and hold it straight over your torso with your elbows in. The arms should be perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.
Now lower the bar down to your lower chest as you breathe in. Keep the elbows in as you perform this movement.
Using the triceps to push the bar back up, press it back to the starting position by extending the elbows as you exhale.
Repeat.
baseInstructions: Set the bench and rack safeties before lifting. Lie with feet planted, hands slightly wider than shoulders, and shoulder blades supported.
Unrack the bar over the chest. Lower it under control to a comfortable chest-level position.
Press back to the starting position, then return the bar securely to the rack after the set.
Optional grip: a reverse, palms-toward-you grip requires a secure unrack, comfortable wrists and elbows, and suitable safeties or a controlled handoff. Select the load for that grip.

Optional reduced range: use a secure board of known height for a controlled touch, or set matching rack pins for a dead-start press. Brace before each press and do not bounce off the board or pins. Keep the board or pin height consistent when comparing sets.

Optional changing resistance: securely attached matched chains add resistance; overhead reverse bands assist the bar. Keep track of bar load, chains or bands, and anchor setup separately because the same bar load can produce different resistance.

candidates.rationale: The chest pass is preceded by a three-point stance and two approach steps. It is an overspecified sports setup for a generic library.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: If retained as guidance, label the approach as a specialist progression. Do not change the standard stationary pass.
candidates.name: Chest Push from 3 point stance
instructions: Begin in a three point stance, squatted down with your back flat and one hand on the ground. Place the medicine ball directly in front of you.
To begin, take your first step as you pull the ball to your chest, positioning both hands to prepare for the throw.
As you execute the second step, explosively release the ball forward as hard as possible.
Use a clear throwing area. Stop after the throw, retrieve the ball, and reset the three-point stance before the next repetition.
baseInstructions: Stand facing a ready partner in a clear passing area, holding a medicine ball at chest height with both hands.
Extend the arms to pass the ball forward from the chest, keeping the stance balanced.
Receive the controlled return with soft elbows, reset the ball at the chest and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Adds elevated feet plus two hand platforms to an airborne push-up, making a very specific three-box version.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The height changes and hand transitions are advanced; the standard should continue landing on the floor without platform transfers.
candidates.name: Feet-Elevated Depth Push-Up
instructions: Use one stable low box for the feet and two stable low boxes for the hands, placed just outside shoulder width on a nonslip floor.

Place the hand boxes just outside of your shoulders, and place your feet on top of the box so that you are in an feet-elevated push-up position, your hands just inside the hand boxes. This will be your starting position.

Begin by bending at the elbows to lower your body, quickly reversing position to push your body off of the ground. As you leave the ground, move your hands onto the hand boxes, bending your elbows to absorb the impact.
Repeat the motion to return to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Take a push-up position with hands just outside shoulder width and the body in a straight line.
Lower under control, then press strongly enough for the hands to leave the floor without adding a clap.
Land softly through the hands and elbows and reset the body alignment before the next repetition.

candidates.rationale: A wide, toes-out dumbbell squat holding one dumbbell in both hands rather than two beside the body.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Stance and load position change but fit a generic dumbbell-squat family. Preserve comfortable foot/knee alignment and note single-dumbbell loading.
candidates.name: Plie Dumbbell Squat
instructions: Hold a dumbbell at the base with both hands and stand straight up. Move your legs so that they are wider than shoulder width apart from each other with your knees slightly bent.
Your toes should be facing out. Note: Your arms should be stationary while performing the exercise. This is the starting position.
Slowly bend the knees and lower your legs until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Make sure to inhale as this is the eccentric part of the exercise.
Press mainly with the heel of the foot to bring the body back to the starting position while exhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise your torso as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Optional depth cue: place a stable bench behind you and touch it lightly before standing. Keep the muscles engaged throughout; do not sit, relax or bounce on the bench.

candidates.rationale: The current instructions are a normal elbow curl performed face-up on a flat bench with arms beside the torso.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Supine support changes shoulder positioning and clearance. Keep standing curls as the main entry and preserve comfortable supported range as optional.
candidates.name: Lying Supine Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Lie face up on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand and arms resting beside the body in a comfortable shoulder position.
Keep the upper arms still and curl the dumbbells by bending the elbows without forcing the shoulders below the bench.
Lower under control within the available range and repeat.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Optional grip and path: use palms facing each other for a hammer curl, palms down for a reverse curl, or a comfortable outward curl path. A hammer curl can also travel toward the opposite shoulder. Keep the upper arms steady and select a load suited to the chosen grip.

When alternating arms, lower one dumbbell under control before curling the other. Each arm completes the selected repetition count; do not treat the combined left-and-right total as that per-arm target.

candidates.rationale: Both move the body by bending and extending the elbows while the torso stays rigid. Body-Up performs the triceps extension from forearms on the floor rather than leaning on a rack bar.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Consider naming the survivor Bodyweight Triceps Extension. The floor version is substantially harder and needs its own optional setup cue.
candidates.name: Body-Up
instructions: Assume a plank position on the ground. You should be supporting your bodyweight on your toes and forearms, keeping your torso straight. Your forearms should be shoulder-width apart. This will be your starting position.
Pressing your palms firmly into the ground, extend through the elbows to raise your body from the ground. Keep your torso rigid as you perform the movement.
Slowly lower your forearms back to the ground by allowing the elbows to flex.
Repeat.
baseInstructions: Position a bar in a rack at chest height.
Standing, take a shoulder width grip on the bar and step a yard or two back, feet together and arms extended so that you are leaning on the bar. This will be your starting position.
Begin by flexing the elbow, lowering yourself towards the bar.
Pause, and then reverse the motion by extending the elbows.

candidates.rationale: A barbell curl with both upper arms against the inner thighs adds a very specific supported setup.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Two arms share one bar and thigh support changes arm position; this is not the one-arm dumbbell concentration curl.
candidates.name: Seated Concentration Barbell Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench and hold a straight barbell with a comfortable underhand grip, supporting the upper arms against the inner thighs.
Curl the bar while keeping the upper arms still.
Lower by extending the elbows through a comfortable range and repeat.
baseInstructions: Stand tall with an underhand grip on the bar.
Bend the elbows while keeping the upper arms near the sides, then lower without swinging the torso.
Optional grip: use an overhand grip for a reverse curl while keeping the upper arms steady. Choose the load for that grip; it may differ from the underhand curl.

candidates.rationale: Both are hinged rows of the loaded landmine end; standing beside it and rowing with one arm can be a supported variation of a generic landmine-row entry.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Meaningful unilateral and stance difference: preserve per-arm counting, balance, and direct-bar grip. Consider naming the survivor Landmine Row before consolidation.
candidates.name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
instructions: Secure one end of a barbell in a landmine and load the free end. Stand beside the loaded end with the knees softly bent.
Bend forward until your torso is as close to parallel with the floor as you can and keep your knees slightly bent.
Now grab the bar with one arm just behind the plates on the side where the weight was placed and put your other hand on your knee. This will be your starting position.

Pull the bar straight up with your elbow in (to maximize back stimulation) until the plates touch your lower chest. Squeeze the back muscles as you lift the weight up and hold for a second at the top of the movement. Breathe out as you lift the weight. Tip: Do not allow for any swinging of the torso. Only the arm should move.

Slowly lower the bar to the starting position getting a nice stretch on the lats. Tip: Do not let the plates touch the floor. To ensure the best range of motion, I recommend using small plates (25-lb ones) as opposed to larger plates (like 35-45lb ones).
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Secure the bar in a landmine attachment and fit a compatible close-grip rowing handle around the loaded end.
Straddle the bar, hinge at the hips and grasp the handle with both hands.
Draw the handle toward the lower ribs, then lower while keeping the trunk still.

candidates.rationale: The same push-up is performed with the feet on an exercise ball.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This adds elevation and instability. Treat it as an optional advanced support setup, not a requirement of Push-up.
candidates.name: Push-Ups With Feet On An Exercise Ball
instructions: Place the feet on a stable exercise ball and the hands slightly wider than shoulder width on the floor.
Keep a straight trunk as you bend the elbows and lower the chest through a comfortable range.
Press back up without letting the hips sag or the ball roll away, then repeat.
baseInstructions: Place hands under or just outside the shoulders and form a straight line from head to heels.
Bend the elbows to lower the chest, then press the floor away without letting the hips sag.
Hand spacing may be narrower or wider within a comfortable range. Keep the hands secure and control the same chest-lowering and pressing motion.

candidates.rationale: Suspension handles replace the floor while the instructions retain the same straight-body lower-and-press action.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep suspension equipment and body angle explicit for anyone using that option; it is not identical in difficulty to a floor push-up.
candidates.name: Suspended Push-Up
instructions: Anchor your suspension straps securely to the top of a rack or other object.

Leaning into the straps, take a handle in each hand and move into a push-up plank position. You should be as close to parallel to the ground as you can manage with your arms fully extended, maintaining good posture.
Maintaining a straight, rigid torso, descend slowly by allowing the elbows to flex.
Continue until your elbows break 90 degrees, pausing before you extend to return to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Place hands under or just outside the shoulders and form a straight line from head to heels.
Bend the elbows to lower the chest, then press the floor away without letting the hips sag.
Hand spacing may be narrower or wider within a comfortable range. Keep the hands secure and control the same chest-lowering and pressing motion.

candidates.rationale: A crunch with the torso supported on an exercise ball; the essential action is still curling the upper torso.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The ball supports the torso and increases available extension, unlike the base existing option supporting only the legs. Preserve that distinction.
candidates.name: Exercise Ball Crunch
instructions: Lie on an exercise ball with your lower back curvature pressed against the spherical surface of the ball. Your feet should be bent at the knee and pressed firmly against the floor. The upper torso should be hanging off the top of the ball. The arms should either be kept alongside the body or crossed on top of your chest as these positions avoid neck strains (as opposed to the hands behind the back of the head position).
Lower your torso into a stretch position keeping the neck stationary at all times. This will be your starting position.

With the hips stationary, flex the waist by contracting the abdominals and curl the shoulders and trunk upward until you feel a nice contraction on your abdominals. The arms should simply slide up the side of your legs if you have them at the side or just stay on top of your chest if you have them crossed. The lower back should always stay in contact with the ball. Exhale as you perform this movement and hold the contraction for a second.
As you inhale, go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Curl the shoulder blades slightly up while keeping the neck relaxed, then lower under control.

Optional setups include arms overhead, soles of the feet together with knees comfortably open, or lower legs supported on a ball. The upper back still curls from the floor; the ball supports the legs, not the torso.
For an unsupported-leg variation, keep the knees bent in a tuck or extend the legs upward and reach toward the feet. Use a range that keeps the neck relaxed and the return controlled.

Optional loading: hold a plate securely against the chest, or use a decline bench with secure leg supports. Change one loading or leverage option at a time; added weight and bench angle change the demand.

candidates.rationale: The hip-extension bridge is performed with the upper back on an exercise ball instead of on the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Upper-back elevation and instability change the setup and range. Keep those explicit if offered as an option; do not call the setups identical.
candidates.name: Physioball Hip Bridge
instructions: Lay on a ball so that your upper back is on the ball with your hips unsupported. Both feet should be flat on the floor, hip width apart or wider. This will be your starting position.
Begin by extending the hips using your glutes and hamstrings, raising your hips upward as you bridge.
Pause at the top of the motion and return to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Press through the feet to lift the hips until the trunk and thighs align, then lower without arching the lower back.
Optional setup cue: gently tilt the pelvis to bring the ribs and pelvis into alignment before lifting the hips. Keep the tilt small rather than forcing the lower back into the floor.

candidates.rationale: A controlled floor-to-standing barbell pull with a clean-specific grip/back-angle setup rather than a catch.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain the clean setup and controlled first-pull purpose as an optional technique note; it is not a full clean.
candidates.name: Clean Deadlift
instructions: Begin standing with a barbell close to your shins. Your feet should be directly under your hips with your feet turned out slightly. Grip the bar with a double overhand grip or hook grip, about shoulder width apart. Squat down to the bar. Your spine should be in full extension, with a back angle that places your shoulders in front of the bar and your back as vertical as possible.

Begin by driving through the floor through the front of your heels. As the bar travels upward, maintain a constant back angle. Flare your knees out to the side to help keep them out of the bar's path.
After the bar crosses the knees, complete the lift by driving the hips into the bar until your hips and knees are extended.
baseInstructions: Stand with the bar over the middle of the feet.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip it, brace the trunk, then stand with the bar close to the legs; reverse the movement to lower.

Optional changing resistance: matched chains or bands anchored below add resistance; overhead reverse bands assist the bar. Use secure attachments clear of the feet and bar path. Keep track of bar load, chains or bands and anchor arrangement separately.

For a deficit variation, stand on a low, stable platform and keep the bar close through the longer pull. Choose a height that allows a controlled starting position and note that height when comparing loads.

candidates.rationale: The written movement is shoulder elevation from a mid-thigh bar position, with a slight hinge and clean-width grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve its quick technical intent and starting hinge as optional notes, while the main shrug stays controlled.
candidates.name: Clean Shrug
instructions: Begin with a shoulder width, double overhand or hook grip, with the bar hanging at the mid thigh position. Your back should be straight and inclined slightly forward.
Shrug your shoulders towards your ears. While this exercise can usually by loaded with heavier weight than a clean, avoid overloading to the point that the execution slows down.
Lower the shoulders and return the bar to the mid-thigh starting position under control before the next repetition.
baseInstructions: Stand with the bar at the thighs and arms straight.
Lift the shoulders toward the ears without rolling them, pause, and lower slowly.

Optional setup: a wider snatch-style grip changes arm position. A bar held behind the thighs is another option only within a comfortable shoulder range and with a secure pickup and return. Keep the lift a controlled shrug, without rolling the shoulders or jerking the bar.

candidates.rationale: This is the floor-to-standing deadlift segment with the wide snatch grip, fitting the policy that grips need not be separate exercises.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Wide grip changes reach and starting position. Retain the first-pull technique purpose and appropriate load; do not confuse it with a complete snatch.
candidates.name: Snatch Deadlift
instructions: The snatch deadlift strengthens the first pull of the snatch. Begin with a wide snatch grip with the barbell placed on the platform. The feet should be directly under the hips, with the feet turned out. Squat down to the bar, keeping the back in absolute extension with the head facing forward.
Initiate the movement by driving through the heels, raising the hips. The back angle should remain the same until the bar passes the knees.
At that point, drive your hips through the bar as you lay back. Return the bar to the platform by reversing the motion.
baseInstructions: Stand with the bar over the middle of the feet.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip it, brace the trunk, then stand with the bar close to the legs; reverse the movement to lower.

Optional changing resistance: matched chains or bands anchored below add resistance; overhead reverse bands assist the bar. Use secure attachments clear of the feet and bar path. Keep track of bar load, chains or bands and anchor arrangement separately.

For a deficit variation, stand on a low, stable platform and keep the bar close through the longer pull. Choose a height that allows a controlled starting position and note that height when comparing loads.

candidates.rationale: Another cable chest press differentiated by a supported incline bench. A lean catalog can collect these setups under Cable Chest Press, although the incline changes the pressing angle.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the incline support, low-pulley setup and changed angle as an optional variation; do not claim flat and incline loads or muscle emphasis are identical.
candidates.name: Incline Cable Chest Press
instructions: Place a supported incline bench between two low cable pulleys. Take both handles before reclining, keep the feet planted, and begin with the handles beside the upper chest and elbows comfortably below shoulder height.
Begin by extending through the elbow, pressing the handles together straight in front of you. Keep your shoulder blades retracted as you execute the movement.
After pausing at full extension, return to the starting position, keeping tension on the cables.
baseInstructions: Position dual pulleys to chest height and select an appropriate weight. Stand a foot or two in front of the cables, holding one in each hand. You can stagger your stance for better stability.
Position the upper arm at a 90 degree angle with the shoulder blades together. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the rest of the body stationary, extend through the elbows to press the handles forward, drawing them together in front of you.
Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.

candidates.rationale: Low-to-high diagonal cable lift is the reverse directional variation of the catalog’s high-to-low cable woodchopper.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Low-to-high and high-to-low need distinct optional instructions and comparable setup notes; do not describe their force directions as identical.
candidates.name: Standing Cable Lift
instructions: Stand side-on to a low cable and hold the handle with both hands near the hip closest to the pulley.
Guide the handle diagonally upward across the body with controlled hip, knee and trunk movement, allowing a comfortable foot pivot.
Return slowly along the same path and complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Set a cable pulley above shoulder height and stand side-on. Hold its handle in both hands near the higher shoulder with the arms comfortably extended.
Draw the handle diagonally down across the body toward the opposite hip while turning through the hips and torso. Allow the feet to pivot with the movement.
Return under control along the same path. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: Same single-arm kettlebell clean to the shoulder, with the next repetition beginning from a hang instead of a full floor reset.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A continuous hang differs from a dead stop. If merged, rename survivor Kettlebell Clean and preserve start/reset choice and existing bottoms-up option.
candidates.name: Kettlebell Hang Clean
instructions: Hold one kettlebell hanging between the legs with the knees softly bent and the hips hinged.
Extend the hips and knees to clean the bell to the shoulder, rotating the hand around the handle as the bell comes close to the body.
Lower to the hanging position under control without placing it on the floor between repetitions. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

Optional balance progression: receive a light bell with its base pointing upward above the fist instead of in the usual rack. Keep the forearm nearly vertical, stop the bell without striking the arm, then lower under control. Retain the same per-side repetition target.
baseInstructions: Place a kettlebell on the floor between the feet. Hinge and bend the knees to take the handle in one hand.
Extend the hips and knees to bring the bell close to the body, rotating the hand around the handle to receive it at the shoulder without letting it strike the forearm.
Lower the kettlebell under control and set it fully on the floor before the next repetition. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: One-arm support is a form progression of Push-up, but it is a recognized skill with a major difficulty difference. Include only if the library intentionally collapses advanced skills.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve per-arm counts, wide-foot stance and progression difficulty. Keeping this separate remains defensible.
candidates.name: Single-Arm Push-Up
instructions: Take a wide-foot push-up stance with one hand supporting the upper body and the other arm held behind the back.
Keep the hips and shoulders controlled as you lower through a comfortable range.
Press back up without twisting abruptly and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Place hands under or just outside the shoulders and form a straight line from head to heels.
Bend the elbows to lower the chest, then press the floor away without letting the hips sag.
Hand spacing may be narrower or wider within a comfortable range. Keep the hands secure and control the same chest-lowering and pressing motion.

candidates.rationale: Two-bell jerk whose receiving stance is split instead of the parallel-foot second dip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Split-foot catch and recovery are a substantial technique difference. Rename to Double Kettlebell Jerk if combining and keep the normal parallel catch as default.
candidates.name: Double Kettlebell Split Jerk
instructions: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in each hand.

Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so, so that the palms face forward. This will be your starting position.
Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.
Immediately reverse direction, driving through the heels, in essence jumping to create momentum.
As you do so, press the kettlebells overhead to lockout by extending the arms, using your body's momentum to move the weights.
Return your feet to the ground in a split fashion, with one foot forward and one foot back.
Keeping the weights overhead, return to a standing position, bringing your feet together. Lower the weights to perform the next repetition.
baseInstructions: Clean two kettlebells to the shoulder rack and stand with the trunk braced.
Dip through the knees and drive the bells upward, then dip again to receive them overhead with arms extended.
Stand tall to complete the catch, lower the bells under control to the shoulder rack and reset before the next repetition. Set them down under control after the set.

candidates.rationale: Both use leg drive and a second bend to receive the bell overhead; split footwork is the special catch arrangement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Split catch and recovery are meaningful technical skills; retain only as optional advanced guidance, with per-arm counting.
candidates.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Split Jerk
instructions: Clean one kettlebell to the shoulder and stand with a balanced stance.
Dip through the knees and drive the bell overhead while moving the feet into a split stance with both knees bent.
Stabilize the overhead position, recover the feet under the hips, then lower the bell to the shoulder. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Hold a kettlebell by the handle. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward. This will be your starting position.
Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.

Immediately reverse direction, driving through the heels, in essence jumping to create momentum. As you do so, press the kettlebell overhead to lockout by extending the arms, using your body's momentum to move the weight. Receive the weight overhead by returning to a squat position underneath the weight. Keeping the weight overhead, return to a standing position.
Lower the weight to perform the next repetition.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

candidates.rationale: Both lift one bell into an overhead catch; this row adds split-foot receiving and recovery.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Split footwork materially changes balance. Preserve it as optional technical guidance rather than silently replacing the ordinary catch.
candidates.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Split Snatch
instructions: Hold one kettlebell below the body with a controlled hip hinge and a balanced stance.
Extend the hips to guide the bell upward, move under it and receive it overhead in a split stance with the arm extended.
Stabilize, recover the feet under the hips and lower the bell under control. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Start with one kettlebell between the feet and hinge at the hips with a braced trunk.
Extend the hips to guide the bell close, then move the hand smoothly around the handle to receive it overhead with the wrist controlled.
Lower under control to the shoulder rack, then hinge to reset the bell. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.

candidates.rationale: A highly specified BOSU-supported low-cable crunch. It can be removed as its own entry if the survivor becomes a general cable-crunch family.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This differs from the rope-at-head kneeling crunch: forward extended arms, two low pulleys, BOSU support and one-cable load logging. Preserve these only as explicit optional setup notes, not the default.
candidates.name: BOSU Cable Crunch
instructions: Place a BOSU trainer dome-up between two low cable handles on a stable surface. Sit low in front of the dome with the lower back supported, feet planted wide, and the same manageable resistance selected on each cable.
Hold one handle in each hand with arms extended forward and steady. Curl the upper torso a small distance upward without bending the elbows or lifting the hips away from the setup.
Lower the torso under control and complete the selected repetitions. Stop the set before changing to another movement; log the resistance selected on one cable when both sides are equal.
baseInstructions: Kneel facing a high cable and hold the rope near the shoulders.
Curl the ribcage toward the pelvis without pulling with the arms, then return slowly.

The crunch may be performed seated on a stable bench or standing with a balanced stance instead of kneeling. Position the body under the high cable so the rope stays near the shoulders, then curl the ribs toward the pelvis without turning the movement into an arm pull or hip hinge.

candidates.rationale: Alternates presses while rotating the palms and bending toward the opposite side. Related alternative: Dumbbell Shoulder Press, already offering alternating presses without a side bend.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The leaning/rotation distinguishes it; removing it need not import that motion into a standard strict press.
candidates.name: See-Saw Press (Alternating Side Press)
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell at each shoulder, palms facing inward and the trunk braced.
Press one dumbbell overhead while rotating that palm forward and making a modest controlled bend toward the opposite side.
Lower that dumbbell to the shoulder as the other presses up with the same wrist rotation. Continue alternating and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.

candidates.rationale: Combines side-lying ball support with a weight plate held against the side of the head. Related alternative: Dumbbell Side Bend, with a different support and resistance position.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The unusual head-adjacent loading and ball setup need not become required form for a standard side bend; preserve original history if removed.
candidates.name: Weighted Ball Side Bend
instructions: To begin, lie down on an exercise ball with your left side of the torso (waist, hips and shoulder) pressed against the ball.

Your feet should be on the floor while your legs are crossed and hanging from the ball. Hold a weighted plate with your right hand directly to the right side of your head. Tip: Make sure the smooth side of the plate is resting against your head.
Place your left arm across your torso so that your palm is on your obliques. There should be a right angle between your left forearm and upper arm. This is the starting position.
Raise the side of your torso up by laterally flexing at the waist while exhaling.
Hold the contraction for a second and slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat the exercise.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

candidates.rationale: A Smith-machine shrug defined by placing the guided bar behind the body. There is no standard Smith shrug entry to absorb it directly.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Barbell Shrugs is a related conventional alternative, not the same machine setup; avoid a false exact merge.
candidates.name: Smith Machine Behind the Back Shrug
instructions: With the bar at thigh level, load an appropriate weight.

Stand with the bar behind you, taking a shoulder-width, pronated grip on the bar and unhook the weight. You should be standing up straight with your head and chest up and your arms extended. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by shrugging your shoulders straight up. Do not flex the arms or wrist during the movement.
After a brief pause return the weight to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before engaging the hooks to rack the weight.

candidates.rationale: The instructions require a bridge on a stability ball while rotating a cable held above the chest, rather than the standard seated Russian Twist.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Russian Twist is a simpler related choice; the ball-supported bridge and cable line are materially different, so an exact merge would be misleading.
candidates.name: Cable Russian Twists
instructions: Connect a standard handle attachment, and position the cable to a middle pulley position.
Lie on a stability ball perpendicular to the cable and grab the handle with one hand. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable.
Grab the handle with both hands and fully extend your arms above your chest. You hands should be directly in-line with the pulley. If not, adjust the pulley up or down until they are.
Keep your hips elevated and abs engaged. Rotate your torso away from the pulley for a full-quarter rotation. Your body should be flat from head to knees.
Pause for a moment and in a slow and controlled manner reset to the starting position. You should still have side tension on the cable in the resting position.
Repeat the same movement for the selected repetitions.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

candidates.category: Calf raise plus small toe lift
candidates.rationale: Alternates a heel raise with a small toe lift while holding a bar on the back. Related alternative: Standing Barbell Calf Raise.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The toe-lift phase is extra ankle work, not a normal calf-raise rep. Consistent with removing small range-of-motion drills, keep ordinary calf raises.
candidates.name: Rocking Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Unrack a light barbell onto the upper back inside a squat rack and stand with the feet flat. Keep the knees softly bent and the bar stable.
Raise both heels, lower them slowly, then lift the toes a small amount while the heels stay grounded.
Lower the toes to finish one repetition. Keep each motion small enough to maintain balance, then rerack the bar at the end.

candidates.rationale: Alternates one front raise and one lateral raise as successive repetitions. Both component exercises already exist: Front Raise and Lateral Raise.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Each bilateral lift is one rep in this row. Prefer the two standard movements rather than preserving an extra combination entry.
candidates.name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
instructions: In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side.
Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights directly in front of you to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating.
Return the weights to your side.
On the next repetition, raise the weights laterally, raising them out to your side to about shoulder height.
Return the weights to the starting position and continue alternating to the front and side.
Count each bilateral lift as one repetition, alternating one front raise with one lateral raise.

candidates.rationale: Sweeps raised arms from side to front (or front to side) before lowering. Related alternatives: Lateral Raise and Front Raise, not equivalent to the horizontal transfer.
