candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The added transfer changes each repetition; remove as a niche combination rather than force it into either simple raise.
candidates.name: Side Laterals to Front Raise
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, a steady trunk and softly bent elbows.
For the first repetition, raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height, move them forward at the same height, then lower.
For the next repetition, raise forward to shoulder height, move the arms out to the sides, then lower. Alternate these controlled paths within the selected total.

candidates.rationale: Alternates forward steps with a two-handle press while dragging a sled, combining locomotion and upper-body pressing in one entry.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Forward Sled Drag with Harness is a related simpler drag, but its harness and absence of presses make it a different task.
candidates.name: Forward Drag with Press
instructions: Attach a rated rope with two handles to the sled. Face away from the sled and hold one handle in each hand.

Begin the movement by moving forward for one step. Leaning forward, extend through the legs and hips to move, pausing with each step to extend through the elbows, pressing your hands forward. Step forward until you return to the start position prepared to press.

candidates.rationale: Adds a sled harness and chain to a bear crawl, producing a specialized resisted crawl combination.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Bear Crawl and Sled Push remain simpler related movements; neither alone is an exact replacement for loaded crawling.
candidates.name: Bear Crawl Sled Drags
instructions: Wearing either a harness or a loose weight belt, attach the chain to the back so that you will be facing away from the sled. Bend down so that your hands are on the ground. Your back should be flat and knees bent. This is your starting position.
Begin by driving with legs, alternating left and right. Use your hands to maintain balance and to help pull. Try to keep your back flat as you move over a given distance.

candidates.rationale: Combines shoulder rotation with an overhead press from upper arms held sideways. Related alternative: Dumbbell Shoulder Press, which omits that rotation drill.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The shoulder-rotation phase is a separate skill; avoid folding the full sequence into the normal press default.
candidates.name: Cuban Press
instructions: Stand holding light dumbbells with the upper arms raised comfortably to the sides and the elbows bent to right angles. Begin with the forearms pointing down.
Keep the upper arms at the same height and rotate at the shoulders until the forearms point upward, using only a comfortable controlled range.
Press overhead, then reverse the press and rotation to the start. Count the complete sequence as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: Pushes explosively between a kettlebell handle and the floor, switching hands. Related alternative: Push-up; not an equivalent explosive transfer.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain this only as archived history; the regular push-up should not require a handle jump.
candidates.name: Plyo Kettlebell Pushups
instructions: Place a stable flat-based kettlebell on the floor. Take a push-up position with one hand holding its handle and the other hand on the floor.
Lower through a comfortable range, then press explosively enough to move across the bell and switch which hand holds its handle.
Land with soft elbows and secure hand contact. Reset the trunk alignment and repeat toward the other side, counting each push-up and hand switch as one repetition.

candidates.category: Floor press / no matching bench entry
candidates.rationale: Extends the user-highlighted floor-press review to its kettlebell version. No active kettlebell bench press exists to absorb it. Dumbbell Bench Press is a related alternative with different equipment and support.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Do not falsely map this to a kettlebell overhead press or claim a dumbbell bench press is mechanically identical.
candidates.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor holding a kettlebell with one hand, with your upper arm supported by the floor. The palm should be facing in.
Press the kettlebell straight up toward the ceiling, rotating your wrist.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position and repeat.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

For an alternating two-bell variation, keep one bell controlled overhead while the other lowers until the upper arm meets the floor and presses back up. Alternate sides without dropping either bell; the existing per-arm repetition target is unchanged.

candidates.rationale: Passes a bell between and around the legs rather than performing a conventional lift. Related alternative: Kettlebell Swing, which is a different hip-hinge exercise.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Its loop-based counting and handoffs are distinct; remove without claiming equivalence to a swing.
candidates.name: Kettlebell Figure 8
instructions: Stand with the feet wider than hip width and hinge slightly while keeping the trunk steady. Hold a light kettlebell in one hand.
Pass the bell between the legs to the opposite hand reaching from behind, then bring it around the outside of that leg.
Repeat the pass around the other leg to trace a complete figure eight. Count a complete loop around both legs as one repetition and keep each hand transfer controlled.

candidates.rationale: Adds an out-and-back cone hop immediately before a short sprint, creating a very specific sequence.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No exact base; a hop plus run-out is one repetition, unlike either component on its own.
candidates.name: Side Hop-Sprint
instructions: Place a low cone beside you with a short clear running lane ahead.
Hop sideways over the cone and back once, then accelerate forward for a short run-out with room to slow down.
Decelerate, walk back and reset. One out-and-back hop plus run-out is one repetition.

candidates.rationale: Requires two matched benches, a dip belt, and a suspended plate between the feet. No active standard belt-squat entry exists. Related alternative: Barbell Squat, which loads the body differently.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Hip-belt loading differs from back-rack loading. Remove this unusually specific apparatus arrangement rather than silently transferring its load or setup to a barbell squat.
candidates.name: Belt Squat on Benches
instructions: Use two matched stable benches rated for the load, positioned so a plate hanging from a dip belt can travel freely between them. Attach the belt and step onto the supports using a setup you can enter and leave under control.
Stand with each foot fully supported. Bend the hips and knees into a comfortable squat while the plate hangs between the benches.
Press through both whole feet to stand without swaying. Lower and remove the load under control before stepping off.

candidates.rationale: Combines a sit-up on an anchored bench with guiding a barbell upward. Related alternative: Sit-up, which lacks the overhead load component.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The anchored setup, bar handoff, and compound sequence are substantive; removal is preferable to automatic exercise equivalence.
candidates.name: Press Sit-Up
instructions: Lie on a bench with the feet secured in a suitable foot anchor. Set a light barbell above the upper chest with a controlled handoff or reachable support.
Raise the torso through a comfortable sit-up while guiding the bar upward, keeping it balanced and avoiding momentum.
Lower the torso and bar under control, then return the bar to its support after the set.

candidates.rationale: Combines a two-hand dumbbell swing with a jump and reset. Related alternatives: Kettlebell Swing or Bodyweight Jump Squat, each omitting part of the sequence.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The jump and implement differ from a standard swing; remove rather than rewrite its records as an equivalent swing.
candidates.name: Dumbbell Jump Swing
instructions: Hold one light dumbbell securely with both hands between the legs. Stand with room overhead and around the body.
Hinge slightly, then extend the hips and knees to make a small jump while guiding the dumbbell upward in a controlled arc. Use only a height you can reverse without losing the grip or torso position.
Land softly and bring the dumbbell close to the torso before resetting the hinge. Count one jump and controlled reset as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: Adds an overhead plate press to an anchored sit-up and stops short of resting on the floor. Related alternative: Sit-Up, without the press; not equivalent.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The press and partial return define a separate combination. Remove as a niche sequence rather than silently map its load to an ordinary sit-up.
candidates.name: Otis-Up
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet secured under a suitable fixed anchor. Hold a weight plate firmly against the upper chest.
Raise the torso in a controlled sit-up while pressing the plate overhead, keeping it balanced rather than throwing it upward.
Return the plate to the chest as you lean back under control, stopping just short of resting on the floor. Complete the selected repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Lying elbow extension with chains clipped to handles is an unusually specific resistance apparatus.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Lying Dumbbell Tricep Extension or Skullcrushers are related options; chain unloading is distinct and should not be relabeled as a free-weight set.
candidates.name: Chain Handle Extension
instructions: You will need two cable handle attachments and a flat bench, as well as chains, for this exercise. Clip the middle of the chains to the handles, and position yourself on the flat bench. Your elbows should be pointing straight up.
Begin by extending through the elbow, keeping your upper arm still, with your wrists pronated.
Pause at the lockout, and reverse the motion to return to the starting position.

candidates.rationale: Presses cable handles attached to loose chains while lying on a bench, using floor contact to unload chain weight.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Dumbbell Bench Press is a related standard option, but chain unloading changes the resistance curve and equipment; no exact survivor exists.
candidates.name: Chain Press
instructions: Begin by connecting the chains to the cable handle attachments. Position yourself on the flat bench in the same position as for a dumbbell press. Your wrists should be pronated and arms perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.
Lower the chains by flexing the elbows, unloading some of the chain onto the floor.
Continue until your elbow forms a 90 degree angle, and then reverse the motion by extending through the elbow to lockout.

candidates.rationale: Adds passing a kettlebell beneath the front thigh during a forward lunge. Related alternative: Dumbbell Lunges, with different equipment and no transfer.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The transfer is a coordination challenge, not necessary lunge form. Keep ordinary loaded lunges instead of importing this extra step.
candidates.name: Lunge Pass Through
instructions: Stand holding one kettlebell beside the body. Step the opposite foot forward into a stable lunge.
Pass the kettlebell beneath the front thigh into the other hand without rounding or twisting the torso.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then alternate legs. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: Requires several widely spaced boxes and a linked one-leg skip onto and off each box; much more specific than a normal box jump.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: It is a distinct coordination drill, not a duplicate Box Jump. Remove only as a catalog scope decision.
candidates.name: Box Skip
instructions: You will need several boxes lined up about 8 feet apart.
Begin facing the first box with one leg slightly behind the other.
Drive off the back leg, attempting to gain as much height with the hips as possible.

Immediately upon landing on the box, drive the other leg forward and upward to gain height and distance, leaping from the box. Land between the first two boxes with the same leg that landed on the first box.
Then, step to the next box and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Moves a bar front-to-back over the head without a full overhead lockout, seated. Related alternative: Overhead Press, not the same front-to-back cycle.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The front-back-front repetition convention and partial path should stay in archived history rather than become a standard press requirement.
candidates.name: Bradford/Rocky Presses
instructions: Sit upright on a bench inside a rack and unrack a light barbell in front of the shoulders. Use a grip that allows the bar to clear the head without moving the torso.
Press the bar only high enough to clear the head and lower it under control behind the shoulders, within a comfortable range.
Press back over the head and return to the front of the shoulders. Count this front-to-back-to-front cycle as one repetition, then rerack when finished.

candidates.rationale: Same unusual front-back-front bar path as the seated Bradford row, in a standing position. Related alternative: Overhead Press; not equivalent.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retire both Bradford entries together rather than consolidating into another niche row that would survive accidentally.
candidates.name: Standing Bradford Press
instructions: Stand in a squat rack with a light barbell held in front at shoulder height, using a comfortable overhand grip.
Press just high enough to guide the bar over the head to the rear position without touching the neck, then reverse the path back to the front.
One front-to-back-to-front cycle is one repetition. Use a controlled comfortable range and rerack after the set.

candidates.rationale: Trains only the shallow upright dip and return of a jerk, with no overhead phase. Related alternative: Split Jerk or Barbell Push Press; not equivalent.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Do not replace its partial dip with a full squat or whole jerk prescription automatically.
candidates.name: Jerk Dip Squat
instructions: This movement strengthens the dip portion of the jerk. Begin with the bar racked in the jerk position, with the shoulders forward to create a shelf and the bar lightly contacting the throat. The feet should be directly under the hips, with the feet turned out as is comfortable.

Keeping the torso vertical, dip by flexing the knees, allowing them to travel forward and without moving the hips to the rear. The dip should not be excessive. Return the weight to the starting position by driving forcefully though the feet.

candidates.rationale: Requires two people back-to-back rotating to hand the ball around them; a specialized partner drill.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No equivalent active standard. Russian Twist is not a mechanically exact replacement.
candidates.name: Medicine Ball Full Twist
instructions: For this exercise you will need a medicine ball and a partner. Stand back to back with your partner, spaced 2-3 feet apart. This will be your starting position.
Hold the ball in front of the trunk. Open the hips and turn the shoulders at the same time as your partner.
For full rotation, you and your partner should twist in the same direction, i.e. counter-clockwise.
Pass the ball to your partner, and both of you can now twist in the opposite direction to repeat the procedure.

candidates.rationale: Squeezes two plates together while extending the arms forward from a standing position. Related alternative: Dumbbell Bench Press for chest training; not the same resistance direction or squeeze task.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Do not merge the standing isometric squeeze component into bench-press form as though they were equivalent repetitions.
candidates.name: Svend Press
instructions: Begin in a standing position.

Press two lightweight plates together with your hands. Hold the plates together close to your chest to create an isometric contraction in your chest muscles. Your fingers should be pointed forward. This is your starting position.
Squeeze the plates between your palms and extend your arms directly out in front of you in a controlled motion.
Pause at the top of the motion, and then slowly return to the starting position.

candidates.rationale: Performs a straight-arm barbell raise while lying face-down on an incline bench, with a floor pickup behind the bench head. Related alternative: Front Raise, with different implement and support.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A niche setup and shoulder angle; do not confuse it with the supine incline dumbbell front raise.
candidates.name: Straight Raises on Incline Bench
instructions: Place a bar on the ground behind the head of an incline bench.
Lay on the bench face down. With a pronated grip, pick the barbell up from the floor, keeping your arms straight. Allow the bar to hang straight down. This will be your starting position.
To begin, raise the barbell out in front of your head while keeping your arms extended.
Return to the starting position.

candidates.rationale: Walking Claw Running Drill rehearses a knee-lift, lower-leg reach and backward foot sweep; unusually specific gait coaching.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Do not merge to Outdoor Walking or Marching in Place as if their instructions and measurement were equivalent.
candidates.name: Walking Claw Running Drill
instructions: Stand tall with space to move forward. Lift one knee comfortably in front of the body while the opposite arm moves forward.
Extend that lower leg slightly, then sweep the foot down and back to contact the ground underneath the body. Step forward and repeat with the other leg.
Continue alternating at a controlled walking pace for the selected time, keeping the torso steady and avoiding a hard stamp.

candidates.rationale: Isolates pendulum running-arm swings in half-kneeling, an unusually specific technique drill for this simplified exercise catalog.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This is not equivalent to running or loaded arm strength work; remove on scope rather than duplicate grounds.
candidates.name: Half-Kneeling Running Arm Drill
instructions: This drill helps increase arm efficiency during the run. Begin kneeling, left foot in front, right knee down. Apply pressure through the front heel to keep your glutes and hamstrings activated.
Begin by blocking the arms in long, pendulum like swings. Close the arm angle, blocking with the arms as you would when jogging, progressing to a run and finally a sprint.
As soon as your hands pass the hip, accelerate them forward during the sprinting motion to move them as quickly as possible.
Switch knees and repeat.
Use the selected duration with each knee forward, maintaining a steady torso.

candidates.rationale: Stacks supine positioning, a sit-up, an overhead throw and one-arm loading into a specialist partner drill.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No exact active base preserves all these mechanics. Retain historical identity if retired.
candidates.name: Supine One-Arm Overhead Throw
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent, facing a ready partner in a clear throwing area. Hold a medicine ball in one hand with the arm extended behind the head through a comfortable range.
Raise the torso in a controlled sit-up as you throw the ball forward toward the partner.
Receive the controlled return, lower to the starting position and reset. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.

candidates.rationale: Combines a sit-up from the floor with a two-hand overhead partner throw; a niche composite rather than a standard press or crunch.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Different from standing overhead throwing. Retire without relabeling old records as the standing exercise.
candidates.name: Supine Two-Arm Overhead Throw
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent, facing a ready partner in a clear throwing area. Hold a medicine ball with both hands behind the head through a comfortable range.
Raise the torso in a controlled sit-up as you throw the ball forward toward the partner.
Receive the controlled return, lower to the starting position and reset before repeating.

candidates.rationale: Uses small alternating wrist turns to roll a straight bar forward and back. Related alternatives: Barbell Wrist Curl and Reverse Wrist Curl, which use different joint actions.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep the rolling-cycle definition in history; this is not equivalent to one wrist-flexion repetition.
candidates.name: Wrist Rotations with Straight Bar
instructions: Stand holding a straight barbell with both hands in an overhand grip, keeping the forearms steady.
Use controlled small wrist turns to roll the bar forward, alternating the hands as needed, then reverse the motion to roll it back.
Count one forward-and-back rolling cycle as one repetition and stop at the selected target.

candidates.rationale: Uses rotational one-arm thrusts into a swinging heavy bag with a controlled return; a narrow apparatus-specific drill.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This is not a normal press, punch or medicine-ball pass. Remove on scope rather than claim an equivalent standard.
candidates.name: Heavy Bag Thrust
instructions: Utilize a heavy bag for this exercise. Assume an upright stance next to the bag, with your feet staggered, fairly wide apart. Place your hand on the bag at about chest height. This will be your starting position.
Begin by twisting at the waist, pushing the bag forward as hard as possible. Perform this move quickly, pushing the bag away from your body.
Receive the bag as it swings back by reversing these steps.
Count one push and controlled reception as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: Starts with both arms extended in a T and pulls them straight down to the sides. This is a niche cable shoulder-adduction pattern.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: It is not the same path as Cable Crossover or a forward-plane Straight-Arm Pulldown; remove rather than assert a false duplicate.
candidates.name: Cable Iron Cross
instructions: Begin by moving the pulleys to the high position, select the resistance to be used, and take a handle in each hand.
Stand directly between both pulleys with your arms extended out to your sides. Your head and chest should be up while your arms form a "T". This will be your starting position.
Keeping the elbows extended, pull your arms straight to your sides.
Return your arms back to the starting position after a pause at the peak contraction.
Continue the movement for the prescribed number of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: This is a hanging tucked-body row that lifts the legs into the bar, not an ordinary feet-supported row. Its unusual setup is a reasonable removal candidate.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No exact active standard. Suspension Row is a simpler alternative but uses different support mechanics, so do not silently merge its history.
candidates.name: Tucked Inverted Bodyweight Row
instructions: Begin by taking a medium to wide grip on a pull-up apparatus with your palms facing away from you. From a hanging position, tuck your knees to your chest, leaning back and getting your legs over your side of the pull-up apparatus. This will be your starting position.
Beginning with your arms straight, flex the elbows and retract the shoulder blades to raise your body up until your legs contact the pull-up apparatus.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

candidates.rationale: The catalog prescribes balancing a barbell in one hand with a training partner while lying on the floor. Related alternative: Barbell Bench Press; that is not an equivalent unilateral balance task.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retire from the main library rather than recommending this unusual bar-balancing setup as a default press option. Preserve its historical identity.
candidates.name: One Arm Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees comfortably bent. Have a training partner help position and balance a barbell in one hand above the chest.
Keep the bar balanced and lower by bending the elbow until the upper arm meets the floor gently, then press back up.
Have the partner help recover the bar after the set. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.

candidates.rationale: Requires a lying squat machine with shoulder pads and a foot platform, a very specific supported squat apparatus.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Leg Press and Hack Squat remain useful related choices, but neither is an exact apparatus match; removal should preserve old workout history.
candidates.name: Lying Machine Squat
instructions: Adjust the lying squat machine to your body size. Lie against the support with the shoulders under its pads and both feet secure on the platform. Release the stops only after taking control of the load.
Bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth while keeping the back supported and the knees in line with the feet.
Press through the whole foot to extend the legs without forcefully locking the knees. Re-engage the machine stops before getting out.

candidates.rationale: Adapts a hang power clean to a Smith machine’s constrained bar path; this is a niche equipment adaptation rather than a standard general-library movement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Hang Clean and Power Clean remain related free-bar options, but their paths and catches are not interchangeable with a guided Smith bar.
candidates.name: Smith Machine Hang Power Clean
instructions: Position the bar at knee height and load it to an appropriate weight.

Take a pronated grip on the bar outside of shoulder width and unhook the bar from the machine. Your arms should be fully extended with your head and chest up. Your elbows should be pointed out with your shoulders back and down. Your hips should be back, loading the tension into the hamstrings. This will be your starting position.
Initate the movement by forcefully extending the hips and knees, accelerating into the bar. Ensure that you keep your arms straight during this part of the motion.
Upon full extension, rebend the hips and knees to lower your receiving position.
Allow the arms to flex at this point, rotating the elbows around the bar to receive it on your shoulders.
Extend through the hips and knees to come to a standing position with the bar racked on your shoulders to complete the movement.

candidates.rationale: Keeps elbows straight and lifts only by protracting shoulder blades off an incline bench. Related alternative: Barbell Incline Bench Press, which includes elbow extension and is not equivalent.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Do not carry this into press instructions as though it were a normal pressing rep; it isolates scapular movement.
candidates.name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
instructions: Lie back on an Incline Bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms straight. This will be your starting position.
While keeping the arms straight, lift the bar by protracting your shoulder blades, raising the shoulders from the bench as you breathe out.
Bring back the bar to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Keeps straight arms while lifting the shoulders off an incline bench, rather than pressing the dumbbells. Related alternative: Incline Dumbbell Press, not an equivalent movement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the distinction between scapular protraction and an elbow-bending press; a niche isolation can be removed without mislabeling it.
candidates.name: Dumbbell Incline Shoulder Raise
instructions: Sit on an Incline Bench while holding a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs.

Lift your legs up to kick the weights to your shoulders and lean back. Position the dumbbells above your shoulders with your arms extended. The arms should be perpendicular to the floor with your palms facing forward and knuckles pointing towards the ceiling. This will be your starting position.
While keeping the arms straight and locked, lift the dumbbells by raising the shoulders from the bench as you breathe out.
Bring back the dumbbells to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Lies chest-down and only retracts the shoulder blades with arms hanging. Related alternative: Dumbbell Incline Row, which adds elbow bending and is not equivalent.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A scapular-only drill should not be folded into a full-row rep without noting loss of the distinct movement.
candidates.name: Middle Back Shrug
instructions: Lie facedown on an incline bench while holding a dumbbell in each hand. Your arms should be fully extended hanging down and pointing towards the floor. The palms of your hands should be facing each other. This will be your starting position.

As you exhale, squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold the contraction for a full second. Tip: This movement is just like the reverse action of a hug, or trying to perform rear laterals as if you had no arms.
As you inhale go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Presses a kettlebell while bending the body away toward the floor and then returns upright. Related alternative: Single-Arm Kettlebell Press, which deliberately keeps the trunk upright.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Distinct historical strength skill; removal simplifies the library but is not a mechanical duplicate merge.
candidates.name: Bent Press
instructions: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder. The wrist should rotate as you do so. This will be your starting position.

Begin by leaning to the side opposite the kettlebell, continuing until you are able to touch the ground with your free hand, keeping your eyes on the kettlebell. As you do so, press the weight vertically by extending through the elbow, keeping your arm perpendicular to the ground.
Return to an upright position, with the kettlebell above your head. Return the kettlebell to the shoulder and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side, returning the kettlebell to a controlled rack position between repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Uses a sled as resistance for overhead triceps extensions and requires stepping forward after each repetition to restore line tension.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Cable Overhead Triceps Extension is a related standard option, but the sled does not provide the same return-phase resistance.
candidates.name: Sled Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach handles to a sled and face away from it with the handles behind the head and elbows bent.
Keep the upper arms controlled as you extend the elbows to draw the sled forward.
Return the arms to the bent-elbow start under control while stepping forward to restore line tension. Complete the selected repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Reverse fly performed by pulling a sled and stepping backward to reset slack. This is a niche apparatus adaptation.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Cable Rear Delt Fly is a related standard option; the sled’s resistance and resetting differ, so do not silently merge the histories.
candidates.name: Sled Reverse Flye
instructions: Attach dual handles to a sled connected by a rope or chain. Load the sled to a light weight.

Face the sled, backing up until there is some tension in the line. Take both handles at arms length at about waist level. Bend the knees slightly and keep your chest and head up. This will be your starting position.
Without flexing the elbow, pull the handles upward and apart, performing a reverse fly with some external rotation. Your palms should be facing forward as you do this.
Return to the starting position, taking a couple steps back to take the slack out of the line.

candidates.rationale: A row that draws a sled forward and requires a backward step to restore line tension after every repetition.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Cable Row is a related standard exercise, but it has a resisted return and no walking reset; retain this distinction if removed.
candidates.name: Sled Row
instructions: Attach dual handles to a sled connected by a rope or chain. Load the sled to an appropriate weight. Face the sled, backing up until there is some tension in the line.
With a handle in each hand, bend the knees slightly, keep your head and chest up, and begin with your arms extended.
To initiate the movement, flex the elbow as you retract your shoulder blades, pulling the sled towards you.
Take a step or two back to get tension in the line and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Requires a cambered bar and a raised chest-support bench with full bar clearance. Related alternative: Barbell Row or Dumbbell Incline Row; neither matches all equipment and support.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No ordinary straight-bar replacement has the same required clearance. Remove as specialty equipment scope rather than conceal that requirement.
candidates.name: Lying Cambered Barbell Row
instructions: Lie chest down on a stable bench with enough clearance for a cambered barbell to hang below it. Take a balanced overhand grip with arms extended.
Pull the bar toward the lower chest by bending the elbows and drawing the shoulder blades together without lifting the torso.
Lower under control until the arms extend and repeat the selected repetitions.

candidates.rationale: A crouched three-point sprint start and short run-out, differentiated mainly by sport-specific start mechanics.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Ordinary Outdoor Running does not preserve start-by-start repetitions, so do not merge measurement histories automatically.
candidates.name: Linear 3-Part Start Technique
instructions: Mark a start line with open running space ahead. Take a staggered crouched stance with the rear-side hand near the line and the opposite arm behind you.
Lean forward and push through the legs to accelerate over a short distance that leaves room to slow down.
Decelerate under control, walk back and reset. Count one start and run-out as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: The current instructions use only the fixed Smith frame as hand support during a bodyweight toe raise. The machine is incidental to a small isolated ankle drill.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: It raises the toes toward the shins, not the heels; do not merge into Calf Raise. Removal also fits the earlier preference against small range-of-motion drills.
candidates.name: Smith-Frame Supported Toe Raise
instructions: Place a flat nonslip weight plate beside the fixed frame of a Smith machine. Stand with both heels supported on the plate and the forefeet free, holding the fixed frame lightly for balance.
Keep the heels planted and lift the forefeet toward the shins without bending the knees.
Lower the forefeet slowly through a comfortable range. The frame is hand support; do not carry the Smith bar on the shoulders for this variation.

candidates.rationale: Combines a moving medicine-ball chest pass with an immediate roughly nine-metre sprint and special combined-repetition counting.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Do not rewrite this as a normal chest pass or running distance record; the sequence is distinct.
candidates.name: Chest Push with Run Release
instructions: Begin in an athletic stance with the knees bent, hips back, and back flat. Hold the medicine ball near your legs. This will be your starting position.
While taking your first step draw the medicine ball into your chest.
As you take the second step, explosively push the ball forward, immediately sprinting for 10 yards after the release. Stop after the short run and retrieve the ball only when it is clear to do so.
Count one throw followed by the approximately 9-metre run as one repetition, then reset.

candidates.rationale: Balances the middle of a full barbell in one hand beside the body during a floor lift. Related alternative: Barbell Deadlift; Suitcase Carry shares asymmetric loading but is a different movement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A one-arm long-bar balancing task should not be silently converted to a bilateral deadlift prescription.
candidates.name: Barbell Suitcase Deadlift
instructions: Stand beside the middle of a barbell, with enough space that the plates cannot catch the feet. Bend the hips and knees to grasp the middle of the bar in one hand.
Keep the shoulders level and the bar balanced as you extend the legs and hips to stand.
Lower the bar to the floor under control. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: Squats holding a barbell behind the legs with long arms. Related alternatives: Barbell Squat or Barbell Deadlift, each with different load placement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Do not conflate with the existing hack-squat machine. This behind-body freeweight pattern has no exact standard counterpart.
candidates.name: Barbell Hack Squat
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a barbell behind you at arms length and your feet at shoulder width. Tip: A shoulder width grip is best with the palms of your hands facing back. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip. This will be your starting position.
While keeping your head and eyes up and back straight, squat until your upper thighs are parallel to the floor. Breathe in as you slowly go down.
Pressing mainly with the heel of the foot and squeezing the thighs, go back up as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: The actual exercise is prone on a bench with alternating small straight-leg hip lifts, not the familiar supine abdominal flutter kick.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Do not merge by the alias Flutter Kicks; prone hip extension and supine hip flexion are different movements.
candidates.name: Prone Bench Flutter Kicks
instructions: Lie face down along a stable bench with the hips near its end, the legs extended beyond it and the hands holding the bench.
Lift one straight leg a small amount, then lower it as the other leg lifts, keeping the pelvis supported and the lower back comfortable.
Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: The instructions sweep dumbbells in a large semicircle beside the body while lying on a bench. Related alternatives: Dumbbell Fly or Dumbbell Pullover, neither equivalent to the full sweep.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This is a distinct arm-circle pattern, so remove rather than label it a simple fly duplicate.
candidates.name: Around The Worlds
instructions: Lay down on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms of the hands facing towards the ceiling. Tip: Your arms should be parallel to the floor and next to your thighs. To avoid injury, make sure that you keep your elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now move the dumbbells by creating a semi-circle as you displace them from the initial position to over the head. All of the movement should happen with the arms parallel to the floor at all times. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Reverse the movement to return the weight to the starting position as you exhale.

candidates.rationale: Sits toward the calves from a kneeling position with a bar on the back. Related alternative: Barbell Hip Thrust for hip extension, but support and movement differ.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Not equivalent to a standing squat or hip thrust; preserve historic identity and omit this niche setup from the standard library.
candidates.name: Kneeling Squat
instructions: Set the bar to the proper height in a power rack. Kneel behind the bar; it may be beneficial to put a mat down to pad your knees. Slide under the bar, racking it across the back of your shoulders. Your shoulder blades should be retracted and the bar tight across your back. Unrack the weight.
With your head looking forward, sit back with your butt until you touch your calves.
Reverse the motion, returning the torso to an upright position.

candidates.rationale: The user lies on a bench, braces the soles against a Smith bar, and curls the pelvis while keeping foot contact. It repurposes the machine for a small hip-lift movement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Reverse Crunch is a simpler related pelvic-curl alternative; it does not reproduce the Smith-bar foot setup.
candidates.name: Smith Machine Hip Raise
instructions: Position a bench beneath a lightly loaded Smith bar with safeties set. Lie on the bench, place the soles against the bar and use hand assistance to position and unhook it; keep the knees softly bent.
Hold the machine sides for stability and curl the pelvis to lift the hips a small distance from the bench without losing foot contact.
Return the hips to the bench under control. Use hand assistance to guide the bar onto its hooks before removing the feet.

candidates.rationale: Straddles the bar with one hand ahead and one behind the body. Related alternative: Barbell Deadlift, which does not straddle the bar.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The asymmetrical setup is the defining technique; removal is a library-scope choice, not exact duplication.
candidates.name: Jefferson Squats
instructions: Stand straddling the middle of a barbell with a comfortable wide stance. Bend the hips and knees to grasp the bar with one hand in front and one behind the body.
Keep the arms long, the torso steady and both feet grounded as you extend the legs and hips to stand.
Lower the bar under control, keeping the knees tracking with the feet. Keep the same hand and foot arrangement for the set.

candidates.rationale: Lying on the floor and tossing a ball vertically above the chest is an unusual setup for a general exercise library.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: It differs from a standing partner chest pass in gravity and catching position, so removal is more honest than an exact-duplicate claim.
candidates.name: Supine Chest Throw
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent and hold a medicine ball suitable for controlled throwing and catching against the chest.
Extend both arms to throw the ball vertically to a manageable height above the chest.
Receive it with both hands and soft elbows, then reset at the chest before repeating.

candidates.rationale: A wall-leaning knee-drive cadence drill rather than a general strength exercise; a narrow sports-coaching use.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Wall support and acceleration posture are purposeful. This is a scope removal, not a duplicate of marching in place.
candidates.name: Linear Acceleration Wall Drill
instructions: Lean at around 45 degrees against a wall. Your feet should be together, glutes contracted.
Begin by lifting your right knee quickly, pausing, and then driving it straight down into the ground.
Switch legs, raising the opposite knee, and then attacking the ground straight down.
Repeat once more with your right leg, and as soon as the right foot strikes the ground hammer them out rapidly, alternating left and right as fast as you can.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

candidates.rationale: Practices driving into a split from a preset partial split rather than a full normal jerk. Related alternative: Split Jerk.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep the split-entry drill identity in history; the regular jerk already covers the complete movement.
candidates.name: Jerk Balance
instructions: Unrack a barbell at the front of the shoulders from a squat rack. Use a light technical load and space to step into the split stance.

This drill helps you learn to drive yourself low enough during the jerk and corrects those who move backward during the movement. Begin with the bar racked in the jerk position, with the shoulders forward, torso upright, and the feet split slightly apart.
Initiate the movement as you would a normal jerk, dipping at the knees while keeping your torso vertical, and driving back up forcefully, using momentum and not your arms to elevate the weight.
Keep the rear foot in place, using it to drive your body forward into a full split as you jerk the weight. Recover by standing up with the weight overhead.
Lower the bar to the front rack under control, reset the initial foot position, and repeat. Rerack when finished.

candidates.rationale: Rotates the elbows under a light bar from a scarecrow position into the front rack. Related alternative: Clean.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Only the turnover/rack segment is practiced; it is not a full clean repetition.
candidates.name: Rack Delivery
instructions: Stand holding a light barbell in the scarecrow position: upper arms at shoulder height and forearms hanging down. Use a controlled clean-width hook grip.
Rotate the elbows forward and under the bar, relaxing the grip enough for it to settle gently on the front shoulders without pressing against the throat.
Keep the bar close and return under control to the drill start before repeating.

candidates.rationale: Moves from a forearm plank to a hip pike and back; arguably niche for the desired simplified catalog, though it is a coherent dynamic exercise.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A moving pike is not equivalent to a static Plank. Keeping it with a clearer name Forearm Plank Pike is defensible.
candidates.name: Butt-Ups
instructions: Begin in a forearm plank with the elbows beneath the shoulders and the legs extended. Keep the trunk steady.
Lift the hips to form a pike while keeping the forearms planted and the knees softly extended.
Lower the hips under control to the plank position without letting the lower back sag. Count the lift and return as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: The instructions hold dumbbells out near shoulder height instead of cycling full raises. Related alternative: Lateral Raise.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: An isometric hold differs from dynamic repetitions and may have different prescription semantics. Remove only as a deliberate simplification.
candidates.name: Crucifix
instructions: Stand upright holding one light dumbbell in each hand. Raise your arms out to the sides until they are near shoulder height, keeping the elbows soft.
Hold the selected position briefly without shrugging or leaning, then lower the dumbbells under control. End the hold before your position changes.

candidates.rationale: Swings a sledgehammer to strike a tire, then controls the rebound; requires a dedicated striking setup.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No ordinary resistance exercise reproduces the striking task. Removal is a product-scope choice, not consolidation of a duplicate.
candidates.name: Sledgehammer Swings
instructions: Stand beside a suitable tyre in a clear swinging area and hold the sledgehammer with both hands.
Guide the hammer through a controlled overhead arc and strike the tyre while allowing a comfortable hip and foot pivot.
Control the rebound before resetting. Complete the selected repetitions from each side rather than chasing maximum force.

candidates.rationale: Receives a shoulder-to-overhead jerk in a full overhead squat. Related alternative: Power Jerk or Split Jerk, both with different catches.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Deep squat reception is technically meaningful; flag for simplification rather than claiming it is an ordinary grip or stance tweak.
candidates.name: Squat Jerk
instructions: Standing with the weight racked on the front of the shoulders, begin with the dip. With your feet directly under your hips, flex the knees without moving the hips backward. Go down only slightly, and reverse direction as powerfully as possible. Drive through the heels create as much speed and force as possible, and be sure to move your head out of the way as the bar leaves the shoulders.

At this moment as the feet leave the floor, the feet must be placed into the receiving position as quickly as possible. In the brief moment the feet are not actively driving against the platform, the athlete's effort to push the bar up will drive them down. The feet should move forcefully to just outside the hips, turned out as necessary. Receive the bar with your body in a full squat and the arms fully extended overhead.
Keeping the bar aligned over the front of the heels, your head and chest up, drive throught heels of the feet to move to a standing position. Carefully return the weight to floor.

candidates.rationale: Cradles the bar in the elbow crooks instead of a front- or back-rack position. Related alternative: Front Squat.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The hold, arm loading, and available load differ substantially; removal is a scope choice rather than declaring the lifts interchangeable.
candidates.name: Zercher Squats
instructions: Set a barbell in a squat rack between waist and chest height. Cradle it in the crooks of both elbows and hold the hands together before standing to unrack it.
With the feet comfortably apart, bend the hips and knees into a controlled squat, keeping the torso steady and both feet grounded.
Press through the whole foot to stand, then rerack the bar at the end.

candidates.rationale: Requires a fitted head harness with suspended plate loading for a small neck movement. No general exercise in the current catalog provides an equivalent pattern.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Dedicated neck-strength work is a real distinct category. Removal is a library-scope choice, not a claim that it is merely a stretch or universally unsuitable.
candidates.name: Seated Head Harness Neck Resistance
instructions: Sit on a stable bench with the feet planted and a fitted head harness. Keep the attached load supported by the hands while positioning it, then lean the head and torso slightly forward.
With hands resting on the knees and the torso steady, lower the head through a small comfortable range without requiring chin-to-chest contact, then return under control.
Complete the selected repetitions, then support the load with the hands before removing the harness.

candidates.rationale: Uses heel elevation, hand support, and a backward-leaning torso with a plate at the chest; there is no active plain Sissy Squat to absorb it. Related alternative: Bodyweight Squat, not equivalent.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The knee-dominant leaning pattern is mechanically distinct. Treat removal as deliberate simplification, not a straightforward duplicate merge.
candidates.name: Weighted Sissy Squat
instructions: Stand beside a fixed squat-rack upright and hold it with one hand for balance. Hold a light weight plate against the chest with the other arm.
Raise the heels onto the balls of the feet and bend the knees forward while leaning the torso back as one unit through a small controlled range. Use the hand support to maintain balance.
Extend the knees to return upright, then lower the heels under control. Count one lowering and return as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: Combines a partial lying extension, a shift of the upper arms, and a close-elbow press. Related alternative: Skullcrushers or Barbell Bench Press; neither is the full hybrid.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This is meaningful specialized triceps work, not just a grip change. Do not remap historical reps as mechanically identical.
candidates.name: JM Press
instructions: Position a flat bench in a rack so the bar can be unracked and reracked under control.

Start the exercise the same way you would a close grip bench press. You will lie on a flat bench while holding a barbell at arms length (fully extended) with the elbows in. However, instead of having the arms perpendicular to the torso, make sure the bar is set in a direct line above the upper chest. This will be your starting position.

Now beginning from a fully extended position lower the bar down as if performing a lying triceps extension. Inhale as you perform this movement. When you reach the half way point, let the bar roll back about one inch by moving the upper arms towards your legs until they are perpendicular to the torso. Tip: Keep the bend at the elbows constant as you bring the upper arms forward.
As you exhale, press the bar back up by using the triceps to perform a close grip bench press.
Now go back to the starting position and start over.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Combines a Smith bar across the back with a one-legged pistol squat. This is a distinct advanced combination with no plain Smith single-leg squat survivor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This is a product-scope removal, not a claim that a two-leg Smith Squat is the same exercise; preserve existing personal workout history.
candidates.name: Smith Machine Pistol Squat
instructions: To begin, first set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Step under it and position the bar across the back of your shoulders.
Take the bar with your hands facing forward, unlock it and lift it off the rack by extending your legs.

Move one foot forward about 12 inches in front of the bar. Extend the other leg out in front of you, holding it off the ground. Look forward at all times and maintain a neutral or slightly arched spine. This will be your starting position.
Maintaining good posture, lower yourself by flexing the knee and hip, going down as far as flexibility allows.
Pause briefly at the bottom and then return to the starting position by driving through the heel of your foot, extending the knee and hip.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

candidates.rationale: Receives a clean in a fore-aft split instead of the catalog standard squat catch. Related alternative: Clean.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Split balance and foot recovery are real technical distinctions; removal is an intentional scope decision.
candidates.name: Split Clean
instructions: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take an overhand grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.

Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. Move the weight with control as you continue to above the knees.

Next comes the second pull, the main source of acceleration for the clean. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips. In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight; at the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so.

Receive the bar with the feet split, aggressively moving one foot forward and one foot back. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Bring the feet together as you stand up.

candidates.rationale: Receives the snatch in a split stance instead of the standard overhead squat. Related alternative: Snatch.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain the historical split-style identity; do not automatically treat the squat-catch lift as equivalent.
candidates.name: Split Snatch
instructions: Begin with a loaded barbell on the floor. The bar should be close to or touching the shins, and a wide grip should be taken on the bar. The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed. Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward. The shoulders should be just in front of the bar. This will be the starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through the front of the heels, raising the bar from the ground. The back angle should stay the same until the bar passes the knees.

Transition into the second pull by extending through the hips knees and ankles, driving the bar up as quickly as possible. The bar should be close to the body. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, forcefully pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. The feet should move forcefully to a split position, one foot forward one foot back. Receive the bar with your body as low as possible and the arms fully extended overhead.
Keeping the bar aligned over the front of the heels, your head and chest up, drive through heels of the feet to move to a standing position, bringing your feet together.
Carefully return the weight to floor.

candidates.rationale: Bends the elbows outward and brings dumbbells inward/down toward the upper chest. Related alternative: Lying Dumbbell Tricep Extension, not the same elbow path.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Distinct triceps-extension method; a specialist library could keep it, but a smaller general library can omit it.
candidates.name: Tate Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand above the upper chest, palms facing forward and elbows directed outward.
Keep the upper arms steady and bend the elbows to move the dumbbells inward and down toward the upper chest under control.
Extend the elbows to raise the dumbbells along the same path, then repeat without resting them on the chest.

candidates.rationale: Flips a large tire using a ground lift, knee drive and forward push, with a specialized object.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No exact base exists. This is a distinct conditioning movement; remove only to narrow the product’s equipment scope.
candidates.name: Tire Flip
instructions: Begin by gripping the bottom of the tire on the tread, and position your feet back a bit. Your chest should be driving into the tire.
To lift the tire, extend through the hips, knees, and ankles, driving into the tire and up.

As the tire reaches a 45 degree angle, step forward and drive a knee into the tire. As you do so adjust your grip to the upper portion of the tire and push it forward as hard as possible to complete the turn. Repeat as necessary.

candidates.rationale: Lifts, carries and loads a sandbag onto a platform; this is a multi-stage event rather than a simple gym lift.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Sandbag work can be useful, but this loading event has no direct standard survivor and different repetition conventions from a carry.
candidates.name: Sandbag Load
instructions: Place a sandbag a short clear distance from a stable loading platform. Choose a course and platform height that allow a controlled lift, carry and placement.
Squat or hinge to bring the sandbag close, wrap the arms around it and extend the hips and knees to lift. Walk toward the platform without rushing.
Place the bag securely on the platform. Reset the bag under control before repeating. One carry and placement is one repetition.

candidates.rationale: Laps a heavy stone, raises it to the chest, and loads a platform. This is a distinct specialist event with no standard exercise replacement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep only if the product intends to support stone-loading/strongman athletes; this is scope simplification, not poor-form judgment.
candidates.name: Atlas Stones
instructions: Begin with the atlas stone between your feet. Bend at the hips to wrap your arms vertically around the Atlas Stone, attempting to get your fingers underneath the stone. Many stones will have a small flat portion on the bottom, which will make the stone easier to hold.
Pulling the stone into your torso, drive through the back half of your feet to pull the stone from the ground.
As the stone passes the knees, lap it by sitting backward, pulling the stone on top of your thighs.

Sit low, getting the stone high onto your chest as you change your grip to reach over the stone. Stand, driving through with your hips. Close distance to the loading platform, and lean back, extending the hips to get the stone as high as possible.
Place the stone securely on the loading platform, then step away. Return it to the starting position using a controlled reset appropriate to the platform and stone before the next repetition.

candidates.rationale: Picks up, carries and loads a keg on a platform; the prescribed rep is a full carry and placement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: There is no exact standard survivor. Removing it should not convert old load repetitions into Farmer’s Walk distance.
candidates.name: Keg Load
instructions: Set one keg about 10 metres from a stable loading platform with a clear path between them. Choose a load and platform height you can control.
Tilt the keg enough to grasp a handle and the opposite lower edge, then extend the hips and knees to bring it securely against the chest.
Walk to the platform under control and place the keg securely on it. Count one pickup, carry and placement as one repetition.
Reset the keg using a controlled method before repeating. The selected repetition target counts completed loads, not individual walking steps.

candidates.rationale: Cleans a handled log to the chest and uses leg drive to press it overhead; requires a specialized log implement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Clean and Press is only a related barbell alternative, not an equipment-identical replacement.
candidates.name: Log Lift
instructions: Stand with the log in front of you and take a balanced grip on its handles. Brace the trunk and extend the hips and knees to clean it to the upper chest while keeping it close.
Dip slightly through the knees, then drive through the legs and extend the elbows to press the log overhead. Stabilize with the head and trunk aligned rather than forcing the neck backward.
Lower under control to the chest and then the ground. Complete the selected repetitions, resetting the stance and brace each time.

candidates.rationale: Carries a purpose-built loaded yoke on the upper back for distance.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Farmer’s Walk uses loads in the hands and is not the same movement; this is a choice about supporting strongman equipment.
candidates.name: Yoke Walk
instructions: Adjust a purpose-built yoke to shoulder height and load it evenly. Stand beneath the crossbar with it across the upper back and take the side posts to steady the frame.
Extend the legs to lift it, then walk with short controlled steps along a clear course.
Continue for the selected distance, slow down and lower the frame securely to the ground.

candidates.rationale: Moves a hanging bar overhead without rebending the knees to catch it. Related alternative: Snatch.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No-under-squat turnover is a substantive technical difference; remove as a specialized drill, not as a renamed full snatch.
candidates.name: Muscle Snatch
instructions: Begin with a loaded barbell held at the mid thigh position with a wide grip. The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed. Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward. The shoulders should be just in front of the bar. This will be the starting position.

Begin the pull by driving through the front of the heels, raising the bar. Transition into the second pull by extending through the hips knees and ankles, driving the bar up as quickly as possible. The bar should be close to the body.
Continue raising the bar to the overhead position, without rebending the knees.

candidates.rationale: Performs the clean pull and explosive extension without receiving the bar on the shoulders. Related alternative: Clean.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The catch and squat are absent; merging its loads/reps as a complete clean would be misleading.
candidates.name: Clean Pull
instructions: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take an overhand or hook grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.

Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight and elbows out. Move the weight with control as you continue to above the knees.

Next comes the second pull, the main source of acceleration for the clean. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips. In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight; at the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended. Full extension should be violent and abrupt, and ensure that you do not prolong the extension for longer than necessary.

candidates.rationale: Performs the wide-grip snatch pull and extension without an overhead catch. Related alternative: Snatch.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The catch and overhead squat are absent. Keep as a specialist option only if segmented weightlifting training belongs in the library.
candidates.name: Snatch Pull
instructions: Place a barbell on the floor close to the shins and take a wide snatch grip. Bend the hips and knees with the chest lifted and the bar close.
Extend the legs to move the bar past the knees, then extend the hips and ankles to accelerate it upward. Keep the arms long until the shrug at the top.
Guide the bar back to the floor under control and reset before the next repetition.

candidates.rationale: Starts with the bar on the back and dips/drives underneath into an overhead squat. Related alternative: Snatch, which includes a pull from the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A specialized receiving drill; removing it sacrifices practice segmentation, not duplicate whole-lift coverage.
candidates.name: Heaving Snatch Balance
instructions: This drill helps you learn the snatch. Begin by holding a light weight across the back of the shoulders. Your feet should be slightly wider than hip width apart with the feet turned out, the same position that you would perform a squat with.
Begin by dipping with the knees slightly, and popping back up to briefly unload the bar. Drive yourself underneath the bar, elevating it overhead as you descend into a full squat.
Return to a standing position.

candidates.rationale: Back-rack dip and drive followed by moving the feet into an overhead-squat catch. Related alternative: Snatch; not the same start or pull.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep normal snatch and overhead-squat entries; do not imply this drill is their identical repetition.
candidates.name: Snatch Balance
instructions: Begin with the feet in the pulling position, the bar racked across the back of the shoulders, and the hands placed in a wide snatch grip.
Pop the bar with an abrupt dip and drive of the knees, and aggressively drive under the bar, transitioning the feet into the receiving position.
Receive the bar locked out overhead near the bottom of the squat. The torso should remain vertical, lowering the hips between the legs.
Continue to descend to full depth, and return to a standing position. Carefully lower the weight.

freeweights: All 211 current freeweight-tagged entries were inspected by name and instruction text; current catalog 2026.09.10 contains 643 active exercises.
Merge means proposed catalog grouping, not a claim that altered support/range/grip has identical mechanics or interchangeable load. Preserve the distinction noted and retain historical identity.
Remove rows use baseId=null. Related alternatives are named explicitly in rationale and are not executable equivalence mappings.

Priority 1: closest form/setup redundancy. Priority 2: unusual setup, nonstandard combination, or specialist shortlist aligned to user anchors. Priority 3: meaningful specialist work needing a deliberate scope decision.

Retained common incline/decline presses, incline curls, standard Bulgarian split squats, chest-supported dumbbell rows, ordinary Olympic lifts, and most unilateral kettlebell fundamentals. No proposal to remove yoga.
Two shoulder external-rotation entries and finger curls are weighted strength isolation rather than merely stretches; their removal is only a niche-library preference decision.
No proposed survivor is itself a candidate in this file. No catalog, manifest, media, or review session was changed.
machines: Inspected the current 643-entry catalog and compared candidate instructions with active survivors. No catalog or media records changed.

Preserved ordinary Smith bench/incline/overhead press, Smith squat/row/calf raise, machine chest/shoulder press, leg curl, hack squat, leverage deadlift/shrug and conventional cable strength staples. Those are meaningful equipment choices, not automatically unusual.
Kept leverage incline/decline chest press and high row out of this proposal: their supported machine paths are standard strength options despite distinct angles.
Kept Cable Internal Rotation and External Rotation with Cable: these are resisted movements, so earlier removal of unloaded range-of-motion drills does not automatically authorize their removal.

Priority 3 includes genuinely distinct, established specialist events or direction changes. The rationale frames their removal as a catalog-scope decision rather than claiming incorrect form or exact duplication.
bodyweight: All yoga-tagged exercises were screened and intentionally excluded from removal proposals in accordance with the user preference to keep yoga.

Chair-supported, wall/incline/kneeling push-up, hands-assisted Nordic, band-/foot-assisted pull-up, legs-only Dead Bug, and low-impact cardio regressions remain unflagged: these provide practical accessibility, not merely novelty.
Regular equipment families and familiar distinct movements remain unflagged, including Ring Muscle-Up, Ring Dips, Ball Leg Curl, Pike Push-Up, Handstand Push-Ups, Scissors Jump and Split Jump.
Merge is an editorial consolidation recommendation, not a claim that difficulty, muscle demand or prescription is identical. Preserve the distinctions listed when applying any approved merge.
Remove rows lack a mechanically exact standard: they are specialist scope decisions and must not silently relabel historical logs.
No catalog, media, status, review or credit records changed. This file is a review proposal only.
